papers.title: A Narrowly Tuned Olfactory Receptor in the Sunda Pangolin Identifies 1-Octen-3-One as a Key Chemical Cue in Foraging Behavior.
papers.abstract: The Sunda pangolin (Manis javanica) is considered a critically endangered species, partly due to its highly specialized diet, which consists mostly of ants and termites. Field observations have shown that pangolins rely on olfaction to locate ant and termite nests even from distances of several kilometers. However, the specific chemical signal used to locate food in the field remains unknown. Based on transcriptome sequencing, 1033 olfactory receptors (MjavORs) of M. javanica were identified and analyzed. Four MjavORs (OR118, OR171, OR215, and OR276) were functionally characterized using the Xenopus laevis oocyte system co-expressing CFTR, RTP1, and Gαolf. Notably, MjavOR215 showed a robust response to 1-octen-3-one, a compound released from termite nests. An odorant-binding protein, MjavOBP3, also demonstrated the highest binding affinity for 1-octen-3-one. Behavioral tracking assays confirmed that pangolins are significantly attracted to 1-octen-3-one, a volatile emitted from termite nests (p < 0.05), rather than to volatiles from termites themselves. These results clarify the molecular mechanisms underlying pangolin foraging, demonstrating that volatile from termite nests guide this behavior.

papers.title: Coal Tar-Based Driveway Sealant Extract Induces Mutations in Liver, Bone Marrow, and Germ Cells of MutaMouse Male Mice.
papers.abstract: Coal tar-based driveway sealants (CTS) are a widespread but underrecognized source of human exposure to mutagenic polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). We used Duplex Sequencing, an error-corrected sequencing technology, to assess the mutagenicity of a complex PAH mixture extracted from a CTS in MutaMouse male mice. We observed significant dose-dependent increases in mutation frequency (MF) in liver and bone marrow, with mutation spectra dominated by C:G > A:T substitutions, closely resembling a mutational signature linked to human cancers associated with tobacco smoking. In germ cells, we did not observe a statistically significant increase in MF, although there was a positive dose-response trend and enrichment of C:G > A:T mutations at higher doses. The mutagenic effects of CTS in germ cells were supported by a statistically significant increase in mutant frequency measured using the plaque-based lacZ assay. Tissue-specific analyses revealed greater mutation susceptibility and potency in liver, likely reflecting its central role in PAH metabolism. Mutation spectrum analysis showed that the mutagenic profile of the CTS extract largely resembled that of benzo(a)pyrene; however, detailed spectral analysis indicated additional contributions from other PAHs or PAH metabolites that produced distinct mutational patterns. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that the CTS extract induces tissue-specific mutagenic responses driven by characteristic C:G > A:T mutations, offering mechanistic insight into how environmental PAH mixtures contribute to mutation burden and cancer risk.

papers.title: Flavonoids quercetin and fisetin activate circadian clock and inhibit adipocyte development and hypertrophy.
papers.abstract: The circadian clock maintains temporal control of metabolic processes and plays a key role in adipocyte development. RORα is a circadian clock-regulatory nuclear receptor with diverse metabolic functions. However, the role of the RORα-clock axis in adipocyte biology and its potential as a therapeutic target for obesity remains to be explored. Here, we report how RORα modulation impacts adipocyte development, and identify flavonoid compounds, quercetin and fisetin, as RORα-activating molecules that inhibits adipocyte maturation. Activation of RORα by a synthetic agonist or ectopic expression was sufficient to inhibit adipogenesis. Interestingly, quercetin and fisetin robustly stimulated RORα transcriptional activity and enhanced clock oscillation. Both compounds suppressed preadipocyte differentiation and lipid storage in mature adipocytes that are partially dependent on clock regulation. In vivo administration of quercetin or fisetin resulted in marked RORα induction in adipose depots, accompanied by strong suppression of adipogenic and lipogenic programs. While quercetin attenuated adipocyte hypertrophy with lowering of free fatty acids and improved insulin sensitivity, fisetin displayed a less pronounced effect with differential regulation of lipolytic pathways. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that quercetin and fisetin activate the RORα-clock regulatory axis to suppress adipocyte development, suggesting their potential for clock-targeted interventions in metabolic diseases.

Hypoxic Burden in Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Risk Phenotype for AF Ablation and Ventricular Vulnerability: Hypoxic Burden and Arrhythmia Risk.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is associated with atrial fibrillation (AF), AF recurrence after catheter ablation, and several markers of ventricular electrical vulnerability. The apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) captures respiratory-event frequency but not the cumulative depth and duration of event-related oxygen desaturation. Sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden, the oxygen desaturation index (ODI), T90, and nadir oxygen saturation describe complementary aspects of nocturnal oxygenation. We hypothesized that hypoxic burden complements AHI by quantifying nocturnal oxygenation stress and may support rhythm-focused phenotyping of arrhythmia risk in OSA. This narrative review distinguishes human electrophysiological observations, clinical associations, experimental mechanisms, and hypothesis-generating links. Measurement feasibility, residual exposure after treatment, mapping-related confounding, and prospective validation requirements are examined. Epidemiological studies support associations between sleep-related hypoxemia and cardiovascular outcomes, and human electrophysiological mapping studies show lower atrial voltage and slower conduction in some patients with OSA. However, direct longitudinal evidence linking measured hypoxic burden to serial left atrial substrate change and subsequently to AF recurrence after pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) remains unavailable or insufficient. Trigger-dominant and substrate-dominant recurrence are presented as proposed research constructs, not validated OSA-specific clinical phenotypes or criteria for ablation selection. Hypoxic burden may complement AHI for future rhythm-focused phenotyping, but currently available data do not establish oxygenation-based thresholds or treatment algorithms for AF ablation or ventricular arrhythmia prevention.

papers.title: Polygenic risk scores for sleep: from portability to clinical utility.
Toward a Healthier Future Through Obesity Prevention and Care: The JAMA Summit Report on Obesity.
papers.abstract: Obesity is one of the most difficult challenges of the modern era, affecting more than 1 billion people worldwide. Nearly half of US adults and 1 in 5 US children meet the medical definition of having obesity, with major consequences for cardiometabolic, kidney, hepatic, pulmonary, musculoskeletal, reproductive, oncologic, and mental health. Obesity also carries social and economic harms through stigma, discrimination, and bias. Drivers of the obesity epidemic include changes in food production and consumption accompanied by social, economic, and technological shifts that reduce food preparation, disrupt sleep, and decrease physical activity. The burden of these changes is not equally distributed, with higher obesity prevalence among socioeconomically disadvantaged populations. Current prevention measures include nutrition standards, food and menu labeling, school meal policies, sugar-sweetened beverage taxes, community-based lifestyle programs, and public assistance efforts. The impact of these approaches has been inadequate. Contemporary clinical management recognizes obesity as a chronic disease characterized by genetic, biological, and behavioral susceptibilities. Access, affordability, tolerability, and the chronicity of use remain major challenges for all available obesity management strategies, including new glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist therapies. Potential solutions require a coordinated, multisector response and include efforts to prevent obesity at the societal level, improve care of individuals with obesity, and strengthen research and innovation. Priority areas include improving the food and physical activity environment; strengthening communication and education; strengthening childhood obesity prevention; addressing health inequities; reducing stigma and bias; modernizing obesity care delivery; expanding access to lifestyle, healthy food, medication, and surgical interventions; and supporting long-term treatment adherence and maintenance. Proposed actions include new government policies on food production, labeling, marketing, and school nutrition; modernization of drug evaluation; payment reform to support comprehensive obesity treatment; development of multidisciplinary care models; incentives to promote cross-sector partnerships; and research to advance personalized prevention and treatment strategies. The emergence of effective obesity management medications offers a significant opportunity to curb the prevalence of obesity. However, no single intervention will be enough. Sustained improvement will require addressing the underlying structural and environmental drivers of obesity, along with person-centered, multilevel strategies that simultaneously improve prevention, reduce stigma, and expand equitable access to evidence-based treatment. Coordinated action across government, health care systems, clinicians, payers, industry, schools, communities, and researchers will be essential to achieving long-term improvement.

papers.title: Night work and differential effects on diurnal rhythms of cortisol, melatonin, and testosterone among permanent night-working men.
papers.abstract: Night work-induced circadian misalignment is associated with an increased risk of adverse health effects. It has been suggested that permanent night workers can entrain to being awake at night and therefore do not experience substantial circadian disruption in relation to night work. The aim of this study was to investigate the effects of night work on diurnal rhythms of cortisol, melatonin, and testosterone among permanent night workers. Twenty-three men with permanent night work participated in this observational field study. They collected saliva every 4 hours over a 24-hour period for assessment of diurnal rhythms (mesor, amplitude and acrophase) on three days: the 2nd and 4th consecutive night shifts, and a day off. Within-person regression analyses with repeated measures adjusted for age were used to evaluate differences between the 2nd and 4th night shifts and between night shifts taken together versus days off. There were no statistically significant differences between diurnal rhythms on the 2nd and 4th consecutive night shifts. We observed differences in levels (mesor and amplitude) of cortisol and melatonin on night shifts compared to days off with the highest levels during work days. The timing (acrophase) of testosterone, but not cortisol and melatonin, differed between night shifts and days off. Thus, observed differences between the various hormonal diurnal rhythms to night work indicate internal desynchronization. Studies of how diurnal rhythms of multiple biological systems are affected by night work and the link to health effects are warranted to further elucidate the mechanisms linking night work to adverse health effects.

papers.title: Iron Supplementation as an Adjunctive Treatment for ADHD and Restless Sleep: A Pilot Study.
papers.abstract: The purpose of this study was to examine the impact of oral iron supplementation in youth with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and restlessness during sleep, using both subjective and objective measures of attention and sleep. In this pilot study, 12 youth (M age = 13.56; 67% female) with ADHD, parent reported or self-report of restless sleep, and ferritin levels less than 50 μg/L were treated with 3 months of oral iron supplementation. Before and after treatment, participants completed performance-based measures of attention, parent and self-report ratings of sleep and attention, and 5 nights of at-home actigraphy sleep monitoring. After iron supplementation treatment, participants reported significantly reduced restlessness and sleep disturbance and significant improvements in inattention (1.58 fewer symptoms) and hyperactivity/impulsivity (0.83 fewer symptoms). These subjectively reported improvements were supported by significant objectively measured medium to large effect size improvements in attention. Although mean improvements in objectively measured sleep metrics did not reach statistical significance, night-to-night consistency in wake after sleep onset and periodic limb movements of sleep improved significantly. This pilot study using multiple methods offers preliminary support for the use of oral iron supplementation in treating youth with ADHD, restless sleep, and suboptimal ferritin levels.

papers.title: Adoption of Routine Intraoperative Raw EEG at a Quaternary Pediatric Centre.
papers.abstract: Intraoperative electroencephalography (EEG) allows real-time assessment of the anesthetic state of the brain and offers a means of titrating anesthetic delivery in children. Randomized trials have shown that EEG-guided titration reduces anesthetic exposure, shortens emergence and recovery, and lowers the incidence of emergence delirium, yet routine use outside research settings has remained largely confined to enthusiastic clinicians and clinical trials. To describe the adoption of routine intraoperative raw EEG monitoring over time at a quaternary pediatric hospital, to characterize practice variation among anesthesia providers, and to identify patient and procedural factors associated with EEG use. We conducted a retrospective single-center study of anesthetic records in the electronic health record from 17 October 2024, when automated EEG capture began, to 30 June 2026, following departmental implementation of routine raw EEG monitoring. Providers were categorized by EEG use as high (> 40% of cases), moderate (20%-40%) or low (< 20%). Trend, provider-level, and procedural associations with EEG use were examined using segmented regression, mixed-effects logistic regression, and clustered logistic regression. Of 26 168 analyzed cases, 21.7% (5674) involved intraoperative EEG monitoring, provided by 59 staff anesthesiologists, 9 senior fellows, 24 fellows, and 102 residents. EEG use rose from 17.8% of cases in October 2024 to 28.4% in June 2026. Use varied widely among staff anesthesiologists (median 18.1%, IQR 12.3%-31.3%; range 0.9%-79.5%); 59.3% (35/59) were low users, and 18.6% (11/59) were high users, with the five highest users accounting for 27.0% of all EEG-monitored cases managed by staff. Case mix explained only a small proportion of this variation (pseudo R2 = 0.064). EEG-monitored cases were more often longer, involved neuromuscular blockade, TIVA maintenance, cardiac surgery, and trainee presence. Adoption of routine raw EEG monitoring increased steadily but nonlinearly following implementation. Variation in use among providers was only weakly explained by case mix, indicating that individual practice patterns, more than patient or procedural characteristics, drove uptake. Efforts to broaden EEG monitoring may benefit from targeting low-use providers and during fellowship training.

papers.title: Potentiation of ASIC currents by pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating polypeptide in mouse trigeminal ganglion neurons.
papers.abstract: BackgroundMigraine is a painful neurological disorder. The trigeminal ganglion (TG) neurons are responsible for transmitting pain signals from the head and may play roles in migraine. Various signaling molecules and ion channels, including pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating polypeptide 38 (PACAP-38) and acid-sensing ion channels (ASICs), are expressed in TG neurons and are known to trigger migraine attacks. However, it is still not well understood whether there's a link between them.MethodsElectrophysiological experiments were performed on neurons from mouse TG. Headache behaviors induced by dural injection of PACAP-38 were tested in mice lacking ASIC3.ResultsThe present data showed that PACAP-38 potentiated the electrophysiological function of ASIC3 in mouse TG neurons. PACAP-38 application concentration-dependently increased the density of acid-induced ASIC3 currents. PACAP-38 did not change the pH sensitivity of ASIC3 but increased the maximum responses. The enhancing effect of PACAP-38 on the density of ASIC3 currents was mediated by PAC1 receptors but not by VPAC receptors. The PACAP-induced potentiation was prevented by the protein kinase A (PKA) inhibitor H89 and the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MEK) inhibitor U0126, but not by the protein kinase C inhibitor GF109203X and the p38 inhibitor SB202190, indicating this effect depended on PKA and MEK/extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) signaling. Moreover, PACAP-38 potentiated the burst of action potentials evoked by acidic stimuli. Finally, genetic deletion of ASIC3 ameliorated the facial mechanical hyperalgesia induced by dural injection of PACAP-38 in mice.ConclusionsOur results suggested that PACAP-38 potentiated ASIC3 activity via PAC1 receptors and the PKA and MEK/ERK signaling pathways, which might open promising new perspectives for migraine treatment.

papers.title: Comparison of Infradian and Circadian Rhythms in Laboratory Rodents.
papers.abstract: Infradian cycles are multi-day oscillations whose mechanisms are still poorly understood, while circadian rhythms have been extensively studied and are well-documented in mammals. In this study, we monitored the locomotor activity of three rodent species: CD-1 mice (Mus musculus), Mongolian gerbils (Meriones unguiculatus), and white-tailed antelope squirrels (Ammospermophilus leucurus). We used Lomb-Scargle spectral analysis to verify the prevalence of circadian and infradian rhythms, the magnitude of the spectral power, and associations across species, rhythms, and sexes. Circadian rhythms were robust and were found for all animals. For infradian rhythms, the prevalence in mice was extremely low, whereas the prevalence in gerbils and squirrels was moderate in the 5- and 10-day ranges. In all cases, the strength of infradian rhythmicity was less than 10% of the strength of circadian rhythmicity. As no natural environmental cycle is documented to operate in the 5- to 10-day range, further studies are needed to determine whether an endogenous source may account for this weak but significant infradian rhythmicity.

papers.title: Sleep Deprivation Exacerbates Pulpal Inflammation and Impairs Repair Through Dysregulated Neutrophil Activity in Rats.
papers.abstract: To investigate the effects of sleep deprivation on pulpal inflammation and repair and determine the contribution of neutrophil activity to these changes in rat models. Sleep deprivation was induced in rats using a modified multiple platform method. Pulp responses were evaluated using three experimental settings. Under baseline conditions, rats underwent acute sleep deprivation for four consecutive days. In the inflammatory model, pulpitis was induced by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and assessed 1-4 days after induction. In the reparative model, direct pulp capping (DPC) was performed and pulpal healing was assessed at 14 and 28 days during sleep deprivation. Histological, vascular and inflammatory changes were evaluated by haematoxylin and eosin staining, Masson's trichrome staining, immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence. Transcriptomic alterations in pulp tissue were analysed by mRNA sequencing. Neutrophil abundance and activation were assessed in peripheral blood and dental pulp by complete blood counts, flow cytometry and myeloperoxidase staining. To investigate the functional contribution of neutrophils and neutrophil elastase (NE), sleep-deprived rats were treated with the neutrophil-depleting antibody or the NE inhibitor Sivelestat. Sleep deprivation disrupted pulpal homeostasis, inducing vascular alterations and inflammatory cell infiltration. Following DPC, sleep-deprived rats exhibited impaired repair, including incomplete hard tissue bridge formation and reduced osteopontin expression at Day 14, followed by pulpal necrosis and apical periodontitis at Day 28. In the LPS-induced pulpitis model, sleep deprivation accelerated inflammatory progression and increased pulpal necrosis and leukocyte accumulation. Transcriptomic analysis revealed enrichment of immune- and neutrophil-associated pathways. Sleep deprivation increased neutrophil abundance, accumulation and activation in dental pulp, accompanied by elevated NE expression and enhanced neutrophil extracellular trap-like signals. Neutrophil depletion attenuated pulpal inflammation and tissue injury, while pharmacological inhibition of NE reduced inflammatory responses and pulpal tissue damage. Sleep deprivation exacerbates pulpal inflammation and impairs repair, at least in part through enhanced neutrophil activity and NE-mediated tissue injury. These findings reveal a mechanistic link between sleep disturbance and dysregulated pulpal inflammation and suggest neutrophil/NE-associated pathways as potential targets for further investigation.

papers.title: Chronic Jet Lag Disrupts Cochlear Transcriptome and Induces Immune Dysregulation: Identification of Tripterine as a Potential Modulator.
papers.abstract: Chronic circadian disruption, such as that experienced during jet lag, is associated with various physiological disturbances, yet its molecular consequences in peripheral tissues like the cochlea remain poorly understood. We established a chronic jet lag (CJL) mouse model by subjecting C57BL/6J mice to recurrent 8-hour phase advances of the light schedule over four weeks, while control mice were maintained under a regular 12-hour light/dark cycle. RNA‑seq‑based transcriptomic profiling was performed on cochlear tissues, followed by differential expression analysis, Gene Ontology (GO) and KEGG pathway enrichment, gene set variation analysis (GSVA), and gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA). Immune- and apoptosis-related genes (AIRGs) were identified by intersecting DEGs with immune- and apoptosis-related gene sets. Immune cell infiltration was assessed using ssGSEA. Potential therapeutic compounds were screened using the HERB database, with subsequent molecular docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations performed to validate interactions. A total of 779 DEGs were identified between CJL and LD groups, with 751 upregulated and 28 downregulated genes. Enrichment analyses revealed significant overrepresentation of immune-related processes including adaptive immune response, lymphocyte activation, and cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction. GSVA and GSEA corroborated these findings, demonstrating enhanced activity of inflammatory and immune effector pathways in CJL samples. Twenty-seven AIRGs were identified, with six hub genes (Ccl2, Ccl5, Cd4, Il1b, Il1r2, Tnf) showing significant upregulation. Immune infiltration analysis revealed increased proportions of T cells, NKT cells, and MoDC in CJL samples, with AIRGs exhibiting strong correlations with specific immune cell types. Tripterine was identified as a potential therapeutic compound targeting 23 DEGs, with eight core targets confirmed by molecular docking. MD simulations of the Tripterine-IL1β complex demonstrated stable binding through hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic interactions, and van der Waals forces. Chronic circadian disruption induces profound transcriptional reprogramming in the cochlea, characterized by widespread immune activation and specific alterations in immune cell infiltration. Tripterine shows promise as a modulator of key targets involved in circadian rhythm disturbance.

papers.title: Clinical efficacy of mirabegron in the treatment of female patients with Parkinson's disease and overactive bladder.
papers.abstract: To compare short-term clinical outcomes and adverse events associated with mirabegron and tolterodine treatment in female patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) and overactive bladder (OAB). This retrospective cohort analysis included 90 female patients with PD and OAB treated in Huzhou Third Municipal Hospital from January 2021 to October 2024. The final study cohort comprised 45 patients receiving mirabegron and 45 patients receiving tolterodine, selected in a 1:1 ratio with consideration of available baseline clinical characteristics. The primary efficacy outcome was the change in Overactive Bladder Symptom Score (OABSS) from baseline to 12 weeks. Secondary outcomes included changes in urinary diary variables and the occurrence of adverse events, while changes in the Nonmotor Symptoms Scale (NMSS) and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) were considered exploratory outcomes. A significant group × time interaction was observed for urgency episodes/24 hours (IRR=0.684, 95% CI 0.515-0.908, P=0.009), indicating a greater reduction over time in the mirabegron group. No significant interactions were observed for nocturia episodes/night (IRR=0.938, 95% CI 0.794-1.108, P=0.450) or micturitions /24 hours(IRR=0.962, 95% CI 0.906-1.021, P=0.202). Significant group × time interactions were also observed for OABSS (estimate=-0.422, 95% CI -0.813 to -0.031, P=0.034) and PSQI (estimate=-1.956, 95% CI -3.098 to -0.813, P=0.001), whereas the interaction for NMSS was not significant (estimate=0.244, 95% CI -0.754 to 1.243, P=0.631). There was no significant difference in the incidence of individual adverse events between the two groups after treatment (P>0.05). However, the proportion of patients experiencing at least one adverse event was significantly lower in the mirabegron group than in the tolterodine group (20.0% vs. 44.4%, P=0.013). In this retrospective cohort of female patients with PD and OAB, mirabegron treatment was associated with greater short-term improvements in selected OAB-related outcomes and sleep quality, as well as a lower proportion of patients experiencing adverse events, compared with tolterodine over 12 weeks. These findings require confirmation in prospective randomized studies.

papers.title: Impact of immersive virtual reality combined with lifestyle modification on upper limb function, pain intensity, and range of motion in post-surgical breast cancer survivors: A randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: To compare the effects of immersive virtual reality (VR) and conventional physical therapy (CPT), with or without lifestyle modification (LM), on upper-limb function, pain intensity, and shoulder range of motion (ROM) in post-surgical breast cancer survivors. This four-arm randomized controlled trial (May 2025-April 2026) conducted at Holy Family Hospital Rawalpindi, KINIFIT Physiotherapy, Sehat Pain Management and Physiotherapy Clinic, Islamabad. Sixty women aged 30-60 years, two to four months post-mastectomy/lumpectomy (excluding active/bilateral cancer or lymphoedema), randomized into four groups for eight weeks. VR+LM, VR Only, CPT+LM, or CPT Only. Primary outcomes were pain (Numeric Pain Rating Scale, NPRS) and upper limb function (Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand, DASH). Secondary was shoulder range of motion ROM and lifestyle adherence. NPRS showed a significant Group ×Time interaction( p < .001, partial η² = .262) and large between-group differences at Week 8 (η² = .634); VR+LM achieved the greatest pain reduction. DASH improved significantly within all groups (p < .001), with the largest reduction in CPT+LM and significant between-group differences by Week 8 (η² = .252), interaction was not significant (p = .182). CPT+LM produced the greatest shoulder ROM gains, notably internal rotation. Lifestyle adherence was high for walking, sleep, and breathing (83-90%), low for diet (75%). Virtual Reality with lifestyle modification provided the greatest analgesic benefit, whereas conventional physical therapy with lifestyle modification achieved superior functional and range-of-motion recovery in post-surgical breast cancer rehabilitation. Clinical trial number: NCT07068347.

Drug-resistant epilepsy: A retrospective observational study at a tertiary care hospital.
papers.abstract: To determine the prevalence and predictors of drug-resistant epilepsy among patients with epilepsy. A retrospective observational study was conducted at the Neurology Department of Liaquat National Hospital, Karachi, for the period from November, 2024 to October, 2025. Patients with epilepsy were enrolled, excluding neonates and those with psychiatric comorbidities or active substance abuse. Participants were recruited consecutively. Descriptive statistics summarized patient characteristics, while chi-square tests evaluated associations between variables such as drug adherence, epilepsy type, and antiepileptic drug (ASM) selection. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals were calculated to quantify the strength of these associations. A total of 382 participants were included (49.5% male, 50.5% female), with a mean age of 31.73 +/- 16.82 years and a mean seizure onset age of 25.3 years. The majority were urban residents with higher educational levels and 19.4% had refractory epilepsy. On multivariate logistic regression analysis, normal MRI brain findings (a OR = 0.29, 95% CI: 0.142-0.570; p < 0.001), normal EEG findings (a OR = 0.50, 95% CI: 0.256-0.974; p = 0.042) and adherence to the given treatment (a OR= 0.516, 95% CI: 0.234-1.138; p=0.101) have lower odds of having drug resistance. Lower level of education (a OR = 3.496, 95% CI: 1.687-7.245; p < 0.001), and a history of status epilepticus (a OR = 8.029, 95% CI: 4.186-15.400: p <0.001) have higher odds of refractory epilepsy. By identifying key predictors of drug-resistant epilepsy, our study contributes to a better understanding of factors associated with treatment resistance and may inform future interventions.

papers.title: Implementation Quality and Preliminary Impacts of Compassion-Based Training on Preservice Teachers' Social-Emotional Competencies and Wellbeing: A Propensity Score-Matched Study in Mexico.
papers.abstract: Teachers' social-emotional competencies (SEC) are critical for teacher wellbeing, classroom instruction, and effective student SEL program implementation, yet research on cultivating SEC in preservice teachers remains limited. This mixed-methods, quasi-experimental study evaluated a compassion-based preservice teacher course using propensity score matching. Feasibility analyses indicated that the course was acceptable to PSTs and implementable by instructors. Doubly robust propensity score-matched and weighted hierarchical linear models (n = 354; 177 per group) with false discovery rate correction to control for multiple outcome tests revealed statistically significant effects on perspective-taking (SMD = 0.39, pFDR = .005) and empathic concern (SMD = 0.28, pFDR <. 001). Small, non-significant effects favoring the treatment group were found for self-compassion, flourishing, self-regulation, and sleep quality; while effects on mindfulness, attention regulation, health, sleep quantity, and anxiety were negligible and non-significant. These findings offer initial promising evidence that a compassion-based course can meaningfully cultivate preservice teachers' SEC.

papers.title: Integrating paternal preconception health and sperm molecular biology into proportionate clinical counseling.
papers.abstract: Paternal preconception health increasingly appears to modulate reproductive success through alterations in classical semen parameters and spermatozoal molecular architecture. Beyond nuclear genomic transmission, ejaculated spermatozoa convey regulatory chromatin configurations, retained histones, and diverse small non-coding RNA populations to the oocyte. This narrative review synthesizes evidence across metabolic conditions, lifestyle choices, environmental and occupational toxicant exposures, advanced paternal age, thermal insults, and gonadotoxic therapeutic regimens. Furthermore, emerging considerations regarding psychological strain, circadian misalignment, microplastic accumulation, and male reproductive tract microbial dysbiosis are critically evaluated. We critically synthesize preclinical, epidemiological, and interventional data addressing sperm concentration, motility, morphology, spermatozoal DNA integrity, and coupled clinical endpoints. These clinical benchmarks encompass fertilization efficiency, spontaneous miscarriage, and live-birth rates, alongside documented neurodevelopmental and cardiometabolic trajectories in offspring. Although observational studies link various paternal exposures to impaired semen quality, substantial heterogeneity persists across diverse patient cohorts. Crucially, direct empirical evidence demonstrating that exposure-associated spermatozoal molecular alterations survive post-fertilization reprogramming to cause adverse human phenotypes remains lacking. Postulated mechanistic axes include oxidative stress, systemic inflammation, endocrine disruption, and altered epididymal vesicular signaling, despite incomplete clinical validation. Nevertheless, the 74-90-day window of spermatogenesis and epididymal transit provides an actionable timeline for preconception risk mitigation, rather than a proven "epigenetic reset." We therefore propose an evidence-informed clinical framework delineating guideline-endorsed baseline evaluations and low-risk lifestyle counseling from investigational assays and commercial claims. Importantly, this framework does not assume that paternal exposure-associated sperm epigenetic alterations persist after fertilization, are transmitted across generations, or determine offspring health.

papers.title: Socioeconomic factors associated with multimorbidity among undocumented migrants: A longitudinal study in Geneva, Switzerland.
papers.abstract: Undocumented migrants face intersecting disadvantages that may heighten the prevalence of multimorbidity. This study explores the association between socioeconomic factors and multimorbidity among long-term undocumented migrants in Geneva, Switzerland. We used longitudinal data from the Parchemins study across four waves (2017-2021). Multimorbidity was defined by disease count (≥ two) and by affected body systems (≥ three). Secondary outcomes explored domain-specific health diseases (circulatory, endocrine/metabolic, musculoskeletal, mental). Population-average Poisson regressions adjusted for sex, age, region of origin, and wave assessed associations between the outcomes and socioeconomic, material, psychosocial, behavioral, migration, and structural factors. The prevalence of multimorbidity in waves 1 to 4 were 50.1%, 55.6%, 54.2% and 54.2% using a disease count (≥ two), and 21.0%, 27.3%, 25.0% and 26.9% when based on affected body systems (≥ three). On average, secondary or higher education, the ability to cover unexpected expenses, employment at destination, and cohabitation with a partner were associated with lower prevalence of multimorbidity. In contrast, loneliness and sleep disorders were associated with a higher prevalence of multimorbidity. Participants working in food preparation were at a lower prevalence of multimorbidity and experienced fewer circulatory and musculoskeletal conditions than those in domestic work. Participants who regularized their residence permit had a lower prevalence of mental conditions than those who did not. The prevalence of multimorbidity or of suffering from different conditions that affect the body's systems are associated with factors present in different dimensions of the social structure, with some having a greater influence than others. Policies relying only on treating diseases will fall short unless they address emotional, social, and material insecurity to reduce health inequities.

papers.title: Sleep in school-age children at elevated familial likelihood of autism.
papers.abstract: Clinically significant sleep problems are common in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and can have negative impacts on child cognition, behavior, and health. However, few studies have evaluated sleep in school-aged children with elevated familial likelihood of autism using objective and subjective sleep measures in the home environment. We obtained objective measures of sleep using actigraphy and parent-report of sleep problems using daily sleep diaries and the Children's Sleep Habits Questionnaire. Direct assessment established ASD diagnosis in 7-14-year-old children at higher familial likelihood (HL-ASD n = 39; HL-noASD n = 83) and lower familial likelihood of ASD (LL n = 64). Child sleep problems reported by parents, controlling for age, differed across groups following an endophenotypic pattern (HL-ASD > HL-noASD > LL) and HL-ASD females demonstrated increased sleep problems. Actigraphy and daily sleep diaries did not demonstrate significant group differences. There were significant group differences in psychotropic medication and melatonin use. In one of the first studies to evaluate sleep in school-age children at higher familial likelihood of ASD, parent-report of sleep problems was increased in HL-ASD versus HL-noASD versus LL children. This suggests shared familial influences between ASD and parent-reported sleep problems which could include genetic factors or shared aspects of the home environment. However, sleep characteristics measured objectively by actigraphy and daily sleep diaries revealed a different pattern. Multimodal sleep data can reveal less understood dimensions of sleep patterns in naturalistic home environments and may lead to improved sleep interventions for autistic youth and their siblings.

papers.title: [Dietary Rhythm Disruption and Probiotic Intervention in Metabolic-Associated Fatty Liver Disease: Role of the Bmal1-Gut Microbiota-Liver Axis].
papers.abstract: This study explored how dietary rhythms influence metabolic-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) progression and the interactions among the circadian gene Bmal1, the gut microbiota, and MAFLD. Male Wistar rats were divided into five groups to simulate dietary rhythm disruptions: Control (ad libitum access to the high-fat diet), Control-T, ABX, ABX-FMT, and ABX-B (high-fat diet only during the rest phase). After 17 weeks, the ABX, ABX-FMT, and ABX-B groups received antibiotics to deplete gut microbiota, then ABX-FMT and ABX-B groups followed by fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) from MAFLD patients or Bifidobacterium longum supplementation for 4 weeks, respectively. Metabolic function and MAFLD phenotypes were assessed via physiological measurement and histopathological methods. The expression of gene Bmal1 was evaluated via RT-qPCR and immunohistochemistry, while changes in the gut microbiota were detected by 16S rDNA amplicon sequencing. Compared with the free-feeding Control group, diet rhythm-disrupted rats (Control-T group) showed aggravated hepatic injury, with elevated serum ALT and AST, increased steatosis and inflammation on HE staining, and downregulated hepatic Bmal1 expression. Antibiotic-mediated microbiota depletion (ABX group) markedly altered microbial abundance versus the Control-T group, attenuating hepatic inflammation and steatosis while upregulating Bmal1. Fecal microbiota transplantation from MAFLD patients (ABX-FMT group) increased serum ALT/AST and decreased Bmal1 relative to the ABX group, with reduced phylum-level Firmicutes abundance. Supplementation with Bifidobacterium longum (ABX-B group) alleviated hepatic steatosis and inflammation, lowered ALT/AST and NAS scores, upregulated Bmal1, and increased Verrucomicrobiota while decreasing Firmicutes, Desulfobacterota, and Proteobacteria. Dietary rhythm disruption may be associated with aggravated liver inflammation and steatosis, linked to abnormal expression of the liver circadian gene Bmal1. The gut microbiome may play a crucial role in regulating liver circadian gene expression and metabolic processes through dietary rhythm signals, and probiotic supplementation could help alleviate MAFLD lesions, accompanied by restoration of liver circadian genes and metabolic homeostasis.

papers.title: [Performance Evaluation of a Flexible Sensor-Based Intelligent Monitoring Device for Obstructive Sleep Apnea-Hypopnea Syndrome].
papers.abstract: To evaluate the accuracy of the flexible sensor-based intelligent sleep apnea screening device (TTQ-01) in detecting and diagnosing obstructive sleep apnea hypopnea syndrome (OSAHS) and assessing its severity. Patients with confirmed or suspected OSAHS who met the inclusion criteria underwent simultaneous monitoring with both the TTQ-01 screening device and polysomnography (PSG). PSG findings served as the reference standard. After monitoring, data were anonymized and paired before analysis. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, Cohen's kappa coefficient, and Bland-Altman analysis. For the detection of OSAHS, the TTQ-01 demonstrated an overall accuracy of 97.35% (95% CI: 93.82%-99.10%), a sensitivity of 98.21% (95% CI: 93.82%-99.70%), a specificity of 94.85% (95% CI: 82.67%-98.98%), and a Cohen's kappa coefficient of 0.94 (95% CI: 0.882-0.996), indicating almost perfect agreement with PSG. For the classification of OSAHS severity, the overall agreement rate was 90.07% (95% CI: 85.29%-94.85%), with a sensitivity of 88.39% (95% CI: 82.45%-94.33%), a specificity of 94.87% (95% CI: 82.67%-99.98%), and a Kappa coefficient of 0.825 (95% CI: 0.750-0.900), reflecting strong agreement. Bland-Altman analysis of AHI values measured by TTQ-01 and PSG showed overall unacceptable agreement, with PSG yielding systematically higher values. Subgroup analysis by severity revealed unacceptable agreement in the normal group (with PSG bias elevated), borderline agreement in the mild group, and acceptable agreement in both the moderate and severe groups. The TTQ-01 flexible sensor-based intelligent sleep apnea screening device demonstrated high concordance with PSG in both identifying OSAHS and classifying its severity. In particular, TTQ-01 showed good agreement with PSG among patients with moderate-to-severe OSAHS, suggesting its potential clinical utility as a monitoring and assessment tool in this population. TTQ-01 may serve as a valuable adjunct to support the clinical diagnosis of OSAHS.

papers.title: [Prevalence and Influencing Factors of Comorbidities of Myopia, Overweight and Obesity, and Spinal Curvature Abnormalities Among Primary and Secondary School Students].
papers.abstract: To analyze the comorbidity rates of myopia, overweight and obesity, and spinal curvature abnormalities among primary and secondary school students in Chengdu in 2024, explore the influencing factors of comorbidity, and provide a scientific basis for developing comorbidity prevention and control strategies for common diseases in this population. A stratified cluster random sampling method was employed. Primary and secondary school students from 23 districts under the jurisdiction of Chengdu were randomly selected as study subjects in 2024. Physical examinations and questionnaire surveys were conducted to analyze the comorbidity rates of myopia, overweight and obesity, and spinal curvature abnormalities. The Chi-square test was used to analyze basic characteristics and related factors. A multivariate binary logistic regression model was employed to identify factors associated with comorbidity. A total of 49612 students were included. The detection rate of comorbidity was 18.40%. Multivariate binary logistic regression showed that the risk of comorbidity in males was 1.256 times (95% CI: 1.194-1.322) that in female students.The risk in junior high school, general high school, and vocational high school students was 1.557 times (95% CI: 1.456-1.665), 1.823 times (95% CI: 1.684-1.974), and 1.869 times (95% CI: 1.666-2.097) that of primary school students, respectively. The risk for students engaging in ≥60 min/day of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity was 0.902 times (95% CI: 0.831-0.979) that of those with <60 min/day.The risk for students with insufficient sleep was 1.085 times (95% CI: 1.025-1.148) that of those with adequate sleep. The risk for students whose break-time activity area was outside the classroom but inside the teaching building and outdoors was 0.939 times (95% CI: 0.890-0.990) and 0.841 times (95% CI: 0.768-0.921) that of those staying inside the classroom, respectively. The detection rate of comorbidity is relatively high in Chengdu. Male students, junior high school students, general high school students, and vocational high school students are key populations for comorbidity prevention and control. It is recommended to strengthen health education and promote knowledge on the co-prevention of multiple diseases. Differentiated interventions should be implemented for these key populations, focusing on improving modifiable factors such as physical activity and sleep.

papers.title: [Weight Management Strategies for Children and Adolescents: From Behavioral Correction to Systematic Prevention and Control].
papers.abstract: Overweight and obesity among children and adolescents have become a major public health problem, and the prevention and control strategies are shifting from traditional individual-based behavioral interventions toward systematic, multisectoral collaborative paradigms. Using a three-level nested model of individuals, the environment, and policies as the analytical framework, we systematically summarized in this review the connotation and evidence of Intensive Health Behavior and Lifestyle Treatment (IHBLT). We also analyzed the core challenges, including balancing weight reduction with growth and development, identifying sarcopenic obesity, conducting multi-component assessment of appropriate weight, and understanding the modulatory role of sleep health. The pathways for establishing a multisectoral collaborative system of prevention and control were discussed. On this basis, it was proposed that 3 major scientific questions should be prioritized in future efforts to prevent and control obesity among children and adolescents in China: (1) establishing a localized IHBLT dose-response model to address the challenges of adapting, to local cultural, resource, and technological contexts, the Western standard of 26 or more hours of face-to-face, family-based, multicomponent treatment over a 3- to 12-month period; (2) introducing metabolically healthy obesity (MHO) and metabolically unhealthy obesity (MUO) phenotyping for stratified assessment to avoid overtreatment of children with simple obesity; and (3) using longitudinal data from routine school physical examinations to develop dynamic growth trajectory early-warning algorithms, thereby shifting from single cross-sectional screening to individualized trajectory monitoring. This review aims to provide a reference for building an integrated, full-course management continuum encompassing prevention, screening, diagnosis, treatment, and rehabilitation and for advancing the focus from treating existing disease toward preventing disease before its onset.

papers.title: Diurnal cortisol, perceived sleep quality, actigraphic sleep and depression: an exploratory pilot in patients with head and neck cancer.
papers.abstract: In patients with head and neck cancer (HNC), perceived sleep quality, actigraphy-derived sleep parameters, depressive symptoms, and diurnal cortisol may represent related behavioral and biological processes. This exploratory study tested a priori associations among these constructs. Forty patients with HNC completed the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), wore wrist actigraphs, and collected salivary cortisol at waking and bedtime across a 6-day period. Separate linear regressions tested associations of PSQI scores with actigraphic sleep measures with depressive symptoms, and with cortisol slope, waking, evening and mean indices. Post hoc PSQI item analyses used Spearman correlations. Global PSQI scores were not significantly correlated with actigraphic sleep parameters. Poorer perceived sleep quality was associated with higher depression scores (r = 0.64), flatter diurnal cortisol slopes (r = 0.48), and higher evening cortisol (r = 0.40). Actigraphic sleep parameters were not significantly associated with depressive symptoms or cortisol indices, and depressive symptoms were not significantly associated with cortisol indices. Post hoc item-level analyses showed that poorer overall sleep quality and greater difficulty maintaining enthusiasm were associated with greater depressive symptoms, flatter cortisol slopes, and lower waking cortisol. In this exploratory pilot of patients with HNC, poorer sleep quality was associated with greater depressive symptoms, flatter diurnal cortisol slopes, and higher evening cortisol, whereas actigraphic sleep parameters were not. Global PSQI scores may help identify patients warranting further assessment for depression and treatment-related symptoms.

papers.title: Low-dimensional burnout risk classification in engineering students: the role of demand-recovery interaction features.
papers.abstract: Student burnout is a rapidly growing concern, with prior research linking its development to a wide range of psychological, behavioral, and contextual factors. Machine learning approaches have recently shown strong predictive performance for identifying burnout, but typically rely on high-dimensional datasets impractical for real-world use. Whether burnout can be reliably identified from a minimal set of variables remains underexplored. This study addresses that gap using a low-dimensional predictive framework in undergraduate engineering students. Grounded in Conservation of Resources theory, three classifiers (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting) were evaluated across three feature configurations (Raw: all nine unengineered base predictors, including academic, demographic, sleep, and physical activity variables; Engineered: four demand-recovery interaction features; Full: Raw combined with Engineered) to test whether burnout reflects academic load alone or an imbalance between demand and recovery capacity. The Full configuration performed best: Logistic Regression and Random Forest exceeded a matched permutation-based null (Global MCC = 0.173 and 0.190, respectively, p < 0.05), while Gradient Boosting did not reach significance (MCC = 0.126, p = 0.066). Across 50 alternative fold splits, however, mean Global MCC for the Full configuration was lower for each classifier (Logistic Regression 0.09, Random Forest 0.16, Gradient Boosting 0.11), indicating that the primary-split estimates are upper-range. In addition, adding engineered features to Raw predictors did not produce a statistically distinguishable improvement in Global MCC for any classifier. Moderate Risk classification remained difficult across all classifiers and configurations, with most confidence intervals crossing zero. Permutation importance identified Workload-Sleep Strain as the most influential predictor in the Random Forest model, suggesting the engineered features capture meaningful behavioral patterns. However, because these variables are deterministic transformations of the raw predictors, their incremental contribution could not be confirmed statistically. These results offer preliminary evidence that a small set of sleep, activity, workload, and engineered variables carries predictive signal for burnout risk above chance.

papers.title: Evidence for decoder-label-regime-dependent effects of complementary leaky integrate-and-fire temporal-state decoding in motor-imagery EEG.
papers.abstract: Motor-imagery electroencephalography often provides limited subject-specific supervision. This study tested whether complementary leaky integrate-and-fire (CLIF)-family temporal-state decoding shows a decoder-level advantage after the EEG representation is fixed, how that advantage changes with decoder-label availability, and whether hard binary spikes are required. ANN-SEW, the artificial neural network comparator with spike-element-wise (SEW) residual topology, and SEW-CLIF received identical frozen attention-based temporal convolutional network (ATCNet) and filter-bank convolutional network (FBCNet) representations. The evidence chain combined BCI Competition IV Dataset 2a (BCI2a) development, retrospective OpenBMI replication, an internally pre-access-held-out BCI Competition IV Dataset 2b (BCI2b) evaluation, cross-entropy-only label-budget analyses, and a separate internally pre-access-locked BNCI2015-001 Session-A-to-Session-B evaluation. Additional robustness analyses included shared whole-sequence readout for parameter-matched gated recurrent unit (GRU) and temporal convolutional network (TCN) decoders, exact-gradient sigmoid-gated Soft-CLIF, equal optimizer-update budgets, a within-BCI2a binary sensitivity analysis, and computational profiling. Under cross-entropy-only training, SEW-CLIF exceeded ANN-SEW by 10.082 percentage points (pp) on BCI2a and 5.470 pp. on OpenBMI, while full-budget BCI2b remained near parity (+0.181 pp). The ANN-relative gap decreased as decoder labels increased and persisted under equal-update training. At 25 labels/class, exact-gradient Soft-CLIF exceeded ANN-SEW by 11.085, 8.479, and 5.809 pp. on BCI2a, BCI2b, and OpenBMI, respectively. With matched whole-sequence readout, hard SEW-CLIF was broadly comparable to GRU-Stat and TCN-Stat on BCI2a and BCI2b and modestly higher on OpenBMI. The internally pre-access-locked BNCI2015-001 evaluation showed the same attenuation, with a slope of -2.319 pp. per label doubling (95% CI, -4.118 to -0.604). CLIF-family temporal-state dynamics show a reproducible decoder-label-regime effect under frozen supervised representations. Hard forward discretization is not required for the ANN-relative effect, and matched temporal readout substantially reduces differences between CLIF and other continuous temporal decoders.

papers.title: Longitudinal perspective on the buffering effect of Tai Chi intervention against accumulated perceived stress and its sleep-improving effects among late adolescence.
papers.abstract: First-year university students stand at the close of WHO-defined adolescence (10-19 years), in mid-transition: leaving family, entering a new institution, and assuming adult academic and social roles. Stress during adolescence can have consequences that persist into adulthood. Most mental disorders begin by the mid-twenties, while higher levels of adolescent stress predict greater risks of adult anxiety and depression, academic dropout, and lower workforce participation and productivity. The 16-form simplified Tai Chi routine is easy to learn, but direct evidence of its effect in late adolescents is limited. This randomized controlled trial examined its effect on perceived stress and sleep quality. A total of 176 first-year undergraduates, all aged 18 years at baseline, at a university in Hangzhou, China, were randomly allocated 1:1 to a Tai Chi group (n = 88) or a no-intervention control group (n = 88). The Tai Chi group practiced the 16-form simplified routine three times weekly for 12 weeks (90 min per session: 30 min of warm-up and 60 min of guided practice); controls maintained their usual lifestyle. Perceived stress (Perceived Stress Scale, PSS-14) and sleep quality (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, PSQI) were assessed before and after the intervention. The primary outcomes (PSS-14 and PSQI global scores at week 12) were analyzed by baseline-adjusted analysis of covariance. The groups had similar baseline characteristics. All 176 participants completed the PSS-14 and 168 had complete PSQI data. Within groups, both measures improved under Tai Chi (PSS-14 -3.28; PSQI -1.00; both P < 0.01), whereas perceived stress rose in controls (+4.47, P < 0.001) and sleep quality was unchanged. After baseline adjustment, PSS-14 scores were lower in the Tai Chi group (adjusted mean difference -7.48, 95% CI -8.80 to -6.17; P < 0.001), as were PSQI global scores (-1.17, 95% CI -1.87 to -0.46; P = 0.001). Exploratory component analyses gave nominal P < 0.05 for four PSQI components, none of which remained significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Compared with no intervention, a 12-week 16-form Tai Chi program lowered perceived stress and improved sleep quality in late adolescents starting university, buffering the stress escalation of the academic semester, and merits multicenter testing against an active comparator.

papers.title: Association between sleep patterns and diagnosed chronic kidney disease: a cohort study in China.
papers.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a globally prevalent and progressive health condition, with increasing evidence indicating a significant association between sleep quality and renal health. This study aims to explore the relationship between sleep quality and the development of CKD and to assess how various sleep characteristics influence renal health. This prospective cohort study included participants aged 30-79 years from 10 districts within the China Kadoorie Biobank. Sleep quality was evaluated using a standardized questionnaire that covered seven parameters, including delayed/disrupted sleep, waking early, sleep medication, daytime sleepiness, naps, snoring, and total sleep duration. Different sleep patterns were identified by k-prototype clustering analysis. Survival analysis and relative weight analysis (RWA) were employed to investigate the associations between sleep disturbances and the incidence of diagnosed CKD. Cluster analysis revealed three distinct sleep patterns. Compared with the Cluster1 (optimal sleep), Cluster 2 (frequent napping/snoring) (HR = 1.103, 95% CI: 1.027-1.185, p = 0.007) and Cluster 3 (short and fragmented sleep) (HR = 1.210, 95% CI: 1.129-1.297, p < 0.001) patterns were associated with a significantly increased risk of diagnosed CKD. However, after propensity score matching (PSM), the association for Cluster 2 was attenuated and no longer statistically significant, whereas the association for Cluster 3 remained robust. Of the seven sleep parameters, the top three contributors to diagnosed CKD risk were in order of importance as follows: snoring (RW = 2.59E-04, RS-RW = 55.49%, p < 0.05), total sleep duration (RW = 1.09E-04, RS-RW = 23.32%, p < 0.05), and daytime naps (RW = 4.12E-05, RS-RW = 8.81%, p < 0.05). Unhealthy sleep patterns increased the risk of suffering from diagnosed CKD. Short and fragmented sleep showed the most robust association, whereas the association for frequent napping/snoring was attenuated after PSM. These findings highlight the importance of improving sleep quality and addressing sleep-related problems such as snoring may help reduce diagnosed CKD risk and promote overall kidney health.

papers.title: Screening-positive subclinical eating disorder symptoms and associated factors among high school students: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Subclinical eating disorder (SCED) symptoms are common among adolescents and may be associated with adverse psychological and behavioral outcomes. However, evidence on screening-positive SCED symptoms and associated factors among high school students remains limited. Identifying these factors may support early screening and prevention. In December 2023, a stratified random cluster sampling method was used to recruit students from 12 high schools in Yangzhou, Jiangsu Province, China. Data were collected using a self-developed general information questionnaire, the Eating Disorder Examination Questionnaire 6.0 (EDE-Q 6.0), the Ma Body Figure Scale, the Children's Depression Inventory-Short Form (CDI-S), the Spence Children's Anxiety Scale-Short Version (SCAS-S), the National Mental Health Literacy Questionnaire, and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. BMI was classified using the WHO 2007 age- and sex-specific BMI-for-age reference for participants younger than 19 years, with adult WHO BMI cut-offs used for participants aged 19 years or older. Generalized estimating equations (GEE) with school as the clustering variable were used to examine factors associated with screening-positive SCED symptoms. A total of 2,681 high school students were included in the analysis, of whom 645 (24.1%) screened positive for SCED symptoms. In the school-clustered GEE model, female sex (OR = 1.351, 95% CI: 1.109-1.645), overweight (OR = 3.418, 95% CI: 2.632-4.439), obesity (OR = 7.740, 95% CI: 5.939-10.089), positive body image misperception (OR = 4.280, 95% CI: 3.533-5.184), higher depressive symptom scores (OR per 1-SD increase = 1.454, 95% CI: 1.297-1.630), higher anxiety symptom scores (OR per 1-SD increase = 1.387, 95% CI: 1.269-1.516), and poor sleep quality (OR = 1.393, 95% CI: 1.121-1.733) were associated with higher odds of screening-positive SCED symptoms. Adequate mental health literacy was associated with lower odds (OR = 0.609, 95% CI: 0.506-0.734). Approximately one-quarter of the participating high school students screened positive for SCED symptoms. Screening-positive SCED symptoms were associated with weight status, body image misperception, depressive and anxiety symptom severity, sleep quality, and mental health literacy. These findings support multidimensional school-based screening and health education while recognizing that the EDE-Q threshold identifies a screening-defined condition rather than a clinical diagnosis.

papers.title: Health Burden of Night-Shift Work Among Polysomnography Technologists in India: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Polysomnography technologists perform overnight sleep studies requiring continuous patient monitoring, technical management of diagnostic equipment, and sustained attention. Although night-shift work has been associated with adverse health outcomes among healthcare workers, the occupational health burden among polysomnography technologists remains poorly characterized in India. This study evaluated sleep quality, excessive daytime sleepiness, burnout-related symptoms, musculoskeletal symptoms, and selected cardiometabolic indicators and examined their associations with years of night-shift work experience. This cross-sectional observational study used an online structured questionnaire distributed through professional groups to polysomnography technologists working in private hospitals and sleep centers in South India. Participants were graduates with at least six months of night-shift experience. Of 196 responses, 16 were excluded for less than six months of night-shift experience and 30 for incomplete questionnaires, leaving 150 participants for analysis. The questionnaire included the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS), Copenhagen Burnout Inventory (CBI), and musculoskeletal assessment. Height and weight were measured by participants. Blood pressure was manually assessed, while fasting blood glucose and glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) were obtained from recent laboratory reports. Poor sleep quality was defined as PSQI >5 and excessive daytime sleepiness as ESS >10. The CBI was analyzed continuously and categorized operationally as 0-49, 50-74, and 75-100. Years of night-shift work experience were analyzed as a continuous exposure and categorized as ≤5 versus >5 years. Multivariable logistic regression was adjusted for age, sex, and BMI. Mean age was 29.97 ± 4.43 years, and BMI was 24.16 ± 3.19 kg/m². Mean PSQI, ESS, and CBI scores were 7.09 ± 2.95, 9.20 ± 3.39, and 45.99 ± 20.95, respectively. Poor sleep quality occurred in 97 (64.7%), excessive daytime sleepiness in 56 (37.3%), and musculoskeletal symptoms in 126 (84.0%). CBI scores were categorized as 0-49 in 86 (57.3%), 50-74 in 48 (32.0%), and 75-100 in 16 (10.7%). Hypertension-range blood pressure was identified in 21 (14.0%) and prediabetes in 11 (7.3%). Each additional year of night-shift work experience was associated with higher odds of poor sleep quality (adjusted odds ratio (aOR): 1.433, 95% CI: 1.118-1.835), excessive daytime sleepiness (aOR: 1.205, 95% CI: 1.001-1.450), CBI ≥50 (aOR: 1.810, 95% CI: 1.350-2.428), musculoskeletal symptoms (aOR: 1.372, 95% CI: 1.003-1.878), lower-back symptoms (aOR: 1.296, 95% CI: 1.051-1.598), neck symptoms (aOR: 1.272, 95% CI: 1.043-1.552), and hypertension-range blood pressure (aOR: 1.387, 95% CI: 1.052-1.829). No significant associations were observed with shoulder symptoms or prediabetes. Polysomnography technologists reported frequent poor sleep quality, excessive daytime sleepiness, burnout-related symptoms, and musculoskeletal symptoms. More years of night-shift work experience were associated with several adverse health outcomes after adjustment for age, sex, and BMI. These findings should be interpreted cautiously given the cross-sectional design and potential residual confounding. Prospective multicenter studies are warranted.

papers.title: Associations of insomnia symptoms and physical activity with life satisfaction and psychological well-being among secondary school students in Spain: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Insomnia symptoms and physical inactivity are common during adolescence and may be associated with poorer well-being. However, their independent associations with different well-being indicators remain insufficiently examined in Spanish secondary school students. To examine the independent associations of insomnia symptoms and physical activity with life satisfaction and psychological well-being among adolescents, after adjusting for sociodemographic factors. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 462 secondary school students from six schools in Zaragoza, Spain. Participants completed self-report measures of insomnia symptoms, physical activity, life satisfaction, psychological well-being, and subjective social status. Hierarchical multiple linear regression models with bootstrap confidence intervals were used to examine the contribution of insomnia symptoms and physical activity beyond age, gender, geographical area, and subjective social status. The mean Insomnia Severity Index score was 9.08 (SD = 4.58), and 59.1% of students presented subthreshold, moderate clinical, or severe clinical insomnia symptoms. The mean PAQ-A score was 2.67 (SD = 0.77), with 57.1% of students classified as physically inactive. Insomnia symptoms were negatively associated with both life satisfaction and psychological well-being, whereas physical activity was positively associated with both outcomes. The addition of insomnia symptoms and physical activity increased the explained variance in life satisfaction and psychological well-being beyond sociodemographic covariates. Insomnia symptoms showed larger standardised associations than physical activity in both models. Insomnia symptoms and physical activity were independently associated with well-being indicators among Spanish adolescents. School-based strategies addressing both sleep health and physical activity may contribute to adolescent well-being, although longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to clarify the directionality of these relationships.

papers.title: The impact of nesting care on the growth and neurological development of premature infants in neonatal intensive care units.
papers.abstract: To examine the associations of nesting care with growth, nighttime sleep-wake measures, and early neurodevelopmental outcomes in preterm infants admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU). This single-center retrospective observational study compared two noncontemporaneous cohorts at the Maternal and Child Health Hospital of Linping District, Hangzhou. Fifty preterm infants receiving nesting care from March 2024 to March 2025 and 50 receiving traditional care from February 2023 to February 2024 were manually selected from the eligible population to achieve approximate baseline comparability. Growth was assessed at birth and 3 months corrected age, sleep-wake activity by actigraphy at baseline and day 7, and neurodevelopment using the Gesell Developmental Schedules at 40 weeks postmenstrual age (PMA) and 3 months corrected age. Longitudinal sleep and Gesell outcomes were analyzed using adjusted change-score regression models with HC3 robust standard errors and Holm correction. At 3 months corrected age, the nesting-care group had higher body weight (difference, 195.12 g; 95% CI, 26.00-364.24), greater body length (2.04 cm; 95% CI, 0.68-3.40), and greater head circumference (median difference, 1.00 cm). From baseline to day 7, improvement in total sleep duration was greater in the nesting-care group (adjusted difference in change, 1.09 h; 95% CI, 0.36-1.81; Holm-adjusted P = 0.010), while mean awakening duration decreased more (-0.57 h; 95% CI, -0.70 to -0.45; P < 0.001). For neurodevelopment, adjusted improvements from 40 weeks PMA to 3 months corrected age were greater for fine motor (4.40 points), adaptive (3.95), language (2.18), and personal-social domains (1.60), whereas gross motor change was not statistically significant after adjustment (P = 0.054). In this retrospective comparison of noncontemporaneous cohorts, nesting care was associated with more favorable growth, nighttime actigraphy-derived sleep-wake measures, and several early neurodevelopmental outcomes. These findings should be interpreted cautiously because residual confounding and calendar-period effects cannot be excluded.

papers.title: Mediators of the association between physical activity and depressive symptoms in youth: a systematic review and meta-analytic structural equation modelling.
papers.abstract: Physical activity is consistently associated with fewer depressive symptoms in young people, yet the mechanisms underlying this association remain unclear. This systematic review and meta-analytic structural equation modelling (MASEM) study aimed to identify potential mediators linking physical activity with depressive symptoms in youth and quantitatively synthesise repeatedly examined mediation pathways. Six electronic databases were searched for observational quantitative studies examining physical activity, potential mediators, and depressive symptoms in children, adolescents, and young adults within a prespecified eligibility range of 6-27 years. Potential mediators were synthesised narratively and categorised into conceptually related domains. A random-effects meta-analysis was conducted within the mediation-focused quantitative subset, followed by two-stage random-effects MASEM for mediator constructs with sufficient independent studies and complete correlation data. Eighty-seven studies were included in the broader systematic review, of which 80 formally examined at least one mediator and 39 contributed to the quantitative evidence base. Within this mediation-focused quantitative subset, physical activity was, on average, inversely associated with depressive symptoms (r = -0.234, 95% CI -0.281 to -0.187), although heterogeneity was substantial (I2 = 98.29%) and the 95% prediction interval included zero (-0.499 to 0.070). Narrative synthesis identified potential pathways involving psychological resources and self-related perceptions, social factors, behavioural and lifestyle factors, cognitive-emotional processes, maladaptive behavioural factors, and physical or neurobiological factors. Construct-specific MASEM supported statistical indirect associations through psychological resilience (ab = -0.108, 95% CI -0.172 to -0.061), self-esteem (ab = -0.134, 95% CI -0.239 to -0.062), and social support (ab = -0.127, 95% CI -0.220 to -0.059). Sleep quality showed a significant indirect association in an exploratory model based on three studies. Psychological resilience, self-esteem, and social support emerged as repeatedly examined candidate pathways linking physical activity with depressive symptoms. However, the predominantly cross-sectional and just-identified MASEM models cannot establish temporal ordering, and alternative-direction analyses indicated that at least the resilience correlation structure was also compatible with a reverse indirect pathway. The findings should therefore be interpreted as statistical indirect associations rather than established causal mechanisms. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/recorddashboard, identifier (CRD420261355504).

papers.title: Differential associations of contralesional and ipsilesional brain functional connectivity with lower-limb impairment after stroke.
papers.abstract: Stroke may induce distinct plastic structural changes within the ipsilesional and contralesional hemispheres of the brain, leading to interhemispheric imbalances in cortical connectivity. Maximum joint range of motion (ROMmax) impairments may also occur in the paretic limb, contributing to increased interlimb asymmetry and impaired gait. This study examined the influence of ipsilesional and contralesional brain functional connectivity on hip flexion ROMmax interlimb asymmetry and walking performance in stroke survivors. Eighteen individuals with chronic stroke (57.5 ± 14.8 years; 26.7 ± 22.2 months post-stroke) were assessed for functional connectivity of the ipsilesional and contralesional general hemispheres and specific primary motor cortex (M1) areas of the brain with resting-state electroencephalography (EEG). Participants were also assessed for hip flexion active ROMmax of the paretic and non-paretic limbs and 10-m walk test, and ROMmax interlimb asymmetry was further calculated. Relationships between changes in these variables were examined by Pearson product-moment (r) and regression analyses. Hip flexion ROMmax interlimb asymmetry was significantly associated with contralesional functional connectivity in both general (r = 0.53) and M1-specific (r = 0.48) regions of the brain (P < 0.05). Walking performance was only associated with contralesional M1 connectivity (r = 0.51; P < 0.05). Contralesional hemisphere connectivity explained 28% of the variance in ROMmax asymmetry, while contralesional M1 connectivity explained 26% of the variance in walking time. No significant relationships were found for brain connectivity within the ipsilesional hemisphere. Greater brain functional connectivity in contralesional cortical regions is associated with increased hip ROMmax asymmetry and impaired walking performance in stroke survivors, highlighting the role of contralesional networks in post-stroke motor impairment.

papers.title: Report-derived interictal epileptiform discharge burden is associated with 7-day antiseizure medication decisions after pediatric video electroencephalography.
papers.abstract: To determine whether a three-level interictal epileptiform discharge (IED) burden abstracted from qualitative wording in issued pediatric video electroencephalography (VEEG) reports, rather than directly measured spike frequency, was associated with antiseizure medication (ASM) decisions within 7 days. This single-center retrospective cohort included 216 VEEG report episodes from 181 children. Two reviewers independently classified each report as showing no, low, or moderate-to-high IED burden while unaware of the standardized 7-day outcome; disagreements were adjudicated. We separately analyzed a diagnostic/initiation cohort for new ASM initiation and an established-epilepsy cohort for exploratory treatment intensification. Associations were assessed using exact and trend tests and logistic regression with patient-clustered robust standard errors. Agreement was 211/216 (97.7%); linear-weighted Cohen κ was 0.975 (patient-clustered bootstrap 95% CI 0.947-0.995). The diagnostic/initiation cohort comprised 113 reports from 112 children, with 36 new ASM initiations. Initiation rates were 13.0%, 42.9%, and 70.0% for no, low, and moderate-to-high burden, respectively (trend p < 0.001). The adjusted odds ratio per higher burden grade was 2.89 (95% CI 1.58-5.30; p < 0.001). The established-epilepsy cohort comprised 103 reports from 76 children, with 13 intensification events. Moderate-to-high burden versus none/low yielded an odds ratio of 4.73 (95% CI 1.31-17.08; p = 0.018), but complementary analyses were not statistically significant. Report-derived IED burden showed a strong graded association with new ASM initiation within 7 days. The treatment-intensification finding was exploratory. These data describe prescribing context and do not establish causality, treatment benefit, or an IED-based treatment threshold.

papers.title: Multiple platform-induced sleep restriction disrupts time-of-day-dependent corticosterone and leukocyte profiles in C57BL/6 mice.
papers.abstract: Sleep restriction (SR) is recognized to alter neuroendocrine and immune parameters, yet whether these changes reflect overall alterations in signal magnitude or temporal shifts in systemic dynamics remains poorly defined. We evaluated the effects of subchronic sleep restriction on the 24-h diurnal profiles of serum corticosterone (CS), total white blood cell (WBC) counts, and granulocyte-enriched proportions in mice. Male C57BL/6 mice were subjected to subchronic sleep restriction using the multiple-platform procedure or maintained under control conditions. Serum CS, total circulating WBC counts defined by FSC/SSC gating, and granulocyte-enriched percentages were measured across distinct Zeitgeber times and analyzed using two-way ANOVA with Holm corrections for multiple testing. Daily mean corticosterone levels and total WBC counts did not differ significantly between groups. A significant treatment × time interaction occurred for serum CS (p < 0.001), but time-point differences lost significance after Holm correction (p ≥ 0.06). Total WBC counts showed a borderline interaction (p = 0.050) with no time-point differences post-correction ≥, and CS-WBC correlations were not significant (p > 0.05). Conversely, granulocyte-enriched percentages exhibited a significant interaction (p = 0.002) and retained significant group differences post-correction at ZT5 (36.07 ± 2.57% vs. 18.10 ± 5.59%, adjusted p = 0.005) and ZT11 (53.03 ± 0.21% vs. 84.86 ± 8.64, adjusted p = 0.006). The multiple-platform procedure is associated with time-specific differences in serum CS and granulocyte-enriched percentages without altering the diurnal mean CS or total WBC counts. Lacking direct mechanistic measurements, these data reflect potential temporal variations under sleep restriction paradigms rather than established corticosterone-mediated regulation, clock disruption, or altered tissue homing.
papers.journal: Neurobiology of sleep and circadian rhythms

papers.title: Immediate Return or Overnight Stay? Sleep Responses by Postmatch Travel Strategy and Match Participation in Professional Football.
papers.abstract: Late European away fixtures can disrupt sleep, but the influence of immediate return versus overnight stay, and whether responses differ by match participation, remains unclear. Postmatch travel strategy would influence sleep quality and duration across the prematch, match, and subsequent nights, with responses moderated by match participation. Observational repeated-measures field study. Level 3. A total of 19 outfield English Premier League players were monitored across 10 European away fixtures (5 immediate return and 5 overnight stay).
