Self-reported sleep quality (1 to 7) and sleep duration were recorded on the prematch, match, and subsequent nights. Fixed-effects models examined condition, time, and match participation, with standard errors clustered by player. Sleep quality was lower than prematch baseline on the match and subsequent nights (both β = -0.62 arbitrary units [AU]; P < 0.01; g = -0.63). After overnight stay, sleep quality improved from the match to the subsequent night in players who participated and those who did not (β = 0.69 and 0.63 AU; 95% CIs, 0.37-0.90 and 0.47-0.91; P < 0.01), whereas no change occurred after immediate return. Across participation groups, sleep duration was lower after overnight stay than immediate return on the match night (β = -1.94 hours; P < 0.01; g = -1.26) and subsequent night (β = -1.02 hours; P = 0.02; g = -0.67). However, after overnight stay, sleep duration increased between these nights by 1.45 hours in participants and 1.43 hours in nonparticipants (P < 0.01), with no significant change after immediate return. Participation moderated sleep duration on both postfixture nights (β = 1.27 and 1.64 hours; P ≤ 0.04; g = 0.82 and 1.07). Neither travel strategy was uniformly superior. Overnight stay was associated with poorer absolute sleep duration but a clearer next-night rebound in sleep quality and duration. Postmatch travel should be planned case by case, considering itinerary, next-day demands, and individual match exposure rather than applying a single team-wide policy.

papers.title: Quantifying Menstrual Rhythmicity and Physiological Coherence Using Continuous Wearable Data.
papers.abstract: Continuous wearable data reveal reproducible physiological oscillations across the menstrual cycle. Peripheral temperature offers a physiologically grounded, low-burden signal to align and summarize cycle dynamics at scale, enabling investigation of how reproductive rhythms relate to broader physiological systems. This study aims to introduce a temperature-based cycle coherence score and test whether stronger temperature rhythmicity maps onto known sources of menstrual-cycle variation and relates to cardiorespiratory physiology and sleep. We analyzed nightly wearable data from 150,333 menstrual cycles contributed by 14,536 individuals using Oura Ring. For each cycle, peripheral skin temperature, resting heart rate, heart rate variability, respiratory rate, and sleep duration were modeled using first-harmonic sinusoidal fits scaled to cycle length. We derived a cycle coherence score summarizing the strength, regularity, and temporal organization of temperature-based menstrual rhythms. Mixed-effects models quantified cycle-periodic structure; cycle-level coordination with other signals was assessed via correlations in oscillation amplitude, phase, and fit quality; and participant-level associations between coherence and demographic, anthropometric, and cycle characteristics were evaluated using regression. Peripheral skin temperature exhibited the strongest menstrual-cycle rhythmicity (partial pseudo-R2 = .379, reflecting variance explained by the harmonic terms), forming the basis for a cycle coherence metric capturing substantial cycle-to-cycle variation in rhythm strength, regularity, and timing. Rhythmic variation in other signals was weaker but showed modest coordination with temperature coherence. Mean coherence declined with older age (regression coefficient: β = -0.038 for ≥46 years), higher body mass index (BMI; β = -0.004 per kg/m²), cycle irregularity (β = -0.050), and hormone use (β ≈ -0.082); higher coherence was associated with lower resting heart rate (β = -0.246), lower respiratory rate (β = -0.027), and longer sleep duration (β = 0.062). A temperature-anchored cycle coherence score reflects meaningful variation in menstrual rhythmic organization and demonstrates that stronger temperature rhythmicity coincides with more regulated cardiorespiratory physiology and sleep.

papers.title: Learning and memory profile in pediatric craniopharyngioma with and without associated sleep disturbance.
papers.abstract: Children and adolescents with craniopharyngioma are at increased risk for visual field cuts, endocrinopathies, associated sleep disturbances, and cognitive challenges. While general intellectual functioning tends to remain intact within this population, the sellar/suprasellar location of craniopharyngiomas can disrupt important neural pathways essential for learning and memory. This study examines rote verbal learning and memory profiles - including nuances in learning approaches and slopes - in a clinical sample of pediatric patients treated for craniopharyngioma. Furthermore, the role of sleep disturbance on these outcomes is also explored. Retrospective data were collected for 17 pediatric patients with craniopharyngioma and associated endocrinopathies who underwent neurosurgical resection and irradiation (for all but one). As hypothesized, specific deficits related to rote verbal learning and memory were noted for the sample despite average estimated intellectual and adaptive functioning, while more pronounced learning and memory deficits were observed in the subset with reported sleep disturbances. Learning slope stagnation and/or decline across trials was observed in 75% of the patients, while post-hoc analyses revealed heightened susceptibility to recency effects (with poorer recall from the middle of the list) and a non-statistically significant trend toward increased intrusion errors, despite preserved semantic clustering. Findings underscore the importance of targeted memory assessment and multidisciplinary sleep management in this population.
papers.journal: Child neuropsychology : a journal on normal and abnormal development in childhood and adolescence

papers.title: When impulsivity goes wrong: Circadian timing distinguishes which night shift workers succeed and fail.
papers.abstract: Night-shift workers are at increased risk for accidents and injuries, and extant research has focused predominantly on the effect of sleep loss on low-level cognition as a mechanism. Much less is known about the effects of underlying circadian phase on performance, especially as it relates to accident risk. We assessed whether phase angle between circadian timing (dim-light melatonin onset) and task time predicted impulsivity (i.e. action bias, performance, and strategy) in night shift workers. To do this, we used the Stop Light Task, which simulates the complex, and real-world process drivers go through at a stop light (i.e. whether to stop safely or risk going at a yellow light). Thirty night‑shift workers completed the Stop Light Task approximately 13 h after an 8-h in-lab sleep opportunity, and underwent 24 h of hourly saliva collection to assess dim-light melatonin onset (DLMO). Results showed more time between DLMO and task completion (i.e. greater phase angle) was associated with worse performance (i.e. more crashes) and worse overall strategy in the context of risk. Phase angle did not predict action bias (i.e. propensity to run the yellow light), but post-hoc analyses showed greater sleepiness predicted reduced action bias. These results are the first to show circadian processes directly affect impulsivity in night shift workers and determine when someone is likely to be successful or fail in risky situations.

papers.title: Exploratory Pilot Randomized Crossover Study of Transcutaneous Vagus Nerve Stimulation on Sleep Quality and Mood in Healthy Adults.
papers.abstract: Transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation (tcVNS) has been reported to influence autonomic regulation and sleep in various clinical settings. However, evidence in healthy populations is limited. This study investigated the effects of tcVNS on subjective sleep quality, mood, and autonomic function in healthy adults. We conducted a randomized, double-blind, crossover trial in which 29 healthy participants underwent two four-week stimulation phases (Active and Sham). Active stimulation was delivered at subthreshold intensity, whereas Sham stimulation involved identical device use without electrical current. Outcomes included the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index-Korean version (PSQI-K), Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II), Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAM-D), and daily heart rate variability (HRV) indices collected using a validated smartphone-based application. Linear mixed-effects models were used to analyze questionnaire scores. PSQI-K scores showed a statistically significant but modest reduction during Active stimulation compared with Baseline (P = 0.013) and Sham (corrected P < 0.001), although the mean change did not exceed the minimal clinically important difference. No significant changes were observed for BDI-II or HAM-D. HRV responses were heterogeneous across participants, with no significant group-level differences. No serious adverse events occurred, and mild transient ear discomfort or tingling was reported by 3 participants (10.3%) during Active stimulation. This exploratory pilot trial suggests that tcVNS was safe and well tolerated and may produce modest changes in subjective sleep quality in healthy adults. The absence of mood effects likely reflects low baseline symptom burden. These findings provide preliminary, hypothesis-generating evidence that stimulation parameters may warrant further investigation, and confirmation in adequately powered trials and clinical populations is required. Clinical Research Information Service Identifier: KCT0009790.

papers.title: Validity of Actigraphy and Sleep Diary Compared With Home Polysomnography in Patients With Sleep Apnea and Insomnia Symptoms.
papers.abstract: To evaluate the validity of actigraphy and sleep diaries against home polysomnography (PSG) and to determine whether their performance differs according to sleep apnea and insomnia. Participants underwent one-night home PSG with actigraphy and next-morning sleep diary completion. Parameters included total sleep time (TST), sleep efficiency (SE), sleep latency (SL), and wake after sleep onset (WASO). The apnea subgroup was defined as apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) ≥15, and the insomnia symptoms subgroup as Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index >5 and AHI <15. Mean differences, correlations, correlation comparisons, and agreement with PSG were evaluated. A total of 63 adults (mean age 49.7±14.0 years; 27 male) were included. Overall, actigraphy overestimated TST and SE and underestimated SL, whereas sleep diaries overestimated SL. Both tools were significantly correlated with PSG across all parameters, with sleep diaries showing a stronger correlation with PSG for SL (r=0.817 vs. 0.438, p<0.001). In both the apnea and insomnia symptoms subgroups, actigraphy was significantly correlated with PSG only for TST (ρ=0.594 and 0.462). In contrast, sleep diaries were significantly correlated with PSG for all parameters in the insomnia symptoms subgroup (ρ=0.668-0.781), but only for WASO in the apnea subgroup (ρ=0.440). Both actigraphy and sleep diaries showed validity relative to PSG, but their clinical use should be tailored to the underlying sleep disorder. Sleep diaries may be particularly informative in insomnia, whereas actigraphy may be relatively more useful in sleep apnea.

papers.title: Depression, but Not Anxiety, Is Associated With Poorer Working Memory in Adolescent Psychiatric Patients.
papers.abstract: The present study aimed to examine the associations between depression/anxiety and cognitive functioning in adolescent psychiatric patients to understand the progress of symptoms and build effective intervention plans. Data from 82 adolescents who received psychiatric treatment and psychological assessment at a university hospital were analyzed based on Wechsler Intelligence Scale and the Depression (DEP) and Anxiety (ANX) scales of the Personality Assessment Inventory (PAI). The mean full-scale intelligent quotient was 88.55, which was lower than the normative mean. The mean PAI DEP score was 65.45, and the mean ANX score was 60.10. In the correlation analyses, only DEP and the Working Memory Index (WMI) showed a significant negative correlation(r=-0.24, p=0.005). In a multiple regression analysis in which the three DEP subscales (cognitive, affective, and physiological DEP [DEP-P]) were entered as independent variables and WMI as the dependent variable. Only DEP-P, which assesses symptoms such as sleep problems, reduced activity, and low energy, significantly predicted WMI (β=-0.37, t=-2.90, p=0.005). Adolescent psychiatric patients presenting with a wide range of clinical problems reported more depressive symptoms and showed lower intellectual functioning than normative samples. In addition, the unique association observed between physiological symptoms of depression and working memory is consistent with previous evidence linking these symptoms to circadian rhythm disruption, dysfunction of the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex/frontoparietal network, and white matter deficits. These findings suggest that therapeutic interventions targeting physiological depressive symptoms may contribute to improving working memory and academic achievement in adolescents.

papers.title: Validation of the 14-Item Shortened Version of the Positive and Negative Sleep Appraisal Measure Among Shift-Working Nurses.
papers.abstract: Insomnia is a common condition that significantly impacts physical and mental health. Dysfunctional sleep beliefs and cognitive hyperarousal are recognized as key mechanisms in its development and maintenance. The Positive and Negative Sleep Appraisal Measure (PANSAM) was developed to assess cognitive interpretations of changes in sleep quantity. A shortened version, PANSAM-14, was created using machine learning to enhance clinical usability. This study aimed to evaluate the psychometric characteristics and clinical applicability of PANSAM-14 among shift-working nurses, a high-risk group for insomnia. A total of 299 shift-working nurses from Asan Medical Center completed an online survey including PANSAM-14, Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), and Glasgow Sleep Effort Scale (GSES). Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), item response theory, and Rasch analyses were conducted to assess the construct validity, measurement precision, and item functioning. Reliability and convergent validity were also examined. CFA confirmed the four-factor structure of PANSAM-14 with good model fit indices. Rasch and graded response model analyses supported the measurement precision for most subscales, though subscale 4 showed lower item differentiation and reliability. PANSAM-14 demonstrated high internal consistency and significant positive correlations with ISI, PHQ-9, and GSES. Subscale scores increased in accordance with insomnia severity, supporting the scale's sensitivity and clinical utility. PANSAM-14 demonstrated acceptable psychometric properties for assessing sleep-related cognitive patterns, particularly among shift-working nurses. Its brief structure and acceptable psychometric properties suggest potential utility for clinical and occupational interpretation.

papers.title: Long-Range Temporal Correlations in Brain-State Dynamics via a Multivariate One-Hot Approach.
papers.abstract: Temporal sequences of discrete brain states provide a symbolic representation of large-scale neural dynamics. Here, we introduce a one-hot detrended fluctuation analysis (DFA) formulation to quantify long-range temporal correlations in the recurrence dynamics of individual states, independent of the embedding geometry or the symbolic transition encoding. Applied to resting-state Electroencephalographic microstate sequences acquired under eyes-open (EO) and eyes-closed (EC) conditions, the method reveals heterogeneous scaling exponents across states and a global increase in scaling under EC, indicating condition-dependent modulation of multi-timescale organization. Systematic surrogate manipulations disentangle the structural sources of scaling. Disrupting state lifetime statistics through microstate duration equalization or randomization markedly reduces the Hurst exponent, whereas transition-order shuffling alone produces comparatively minor changes in absolute scaling. These findings indicate that long-range dependence is primarily associated with structured state lifetimes rather than with higher-order symbolic syntax. At the same time, transition ordering modulates EO-EC differences, suggesting that symbolic organization contributes to the context-dependent expression of temporal memory. Combined surrogate operations reveal additive effects. The proposed one-hot formulation provides a minimal, representation-invariant characterization of temporal correlations in symbolic sequences and can be generalized to discrete brain-state dynamics obtained from different neuroimaging modalities.

papers.title: Behavioral Manifestations and Diagnostic Challenges of Restless Legs Syndrome in Infants and Toddlers.
papers.abstract: Restless legs syndrome (RLS) is a sensory-motor neurological disorder, increasingly recognized in children, yet diagnosis in infants and toddlers remains challenging due to the reliance on verbal symptom reporting. This scoping review aims to synthesize the limited literature on probable RLS in infants and toddlers. A structured literature search was conducted using PubMed and Embase from inception through March 2026. Original studies, case reports, case series, and pediatric cohorts reporting probable RLS with onset or evaluation at ≤3 years were included. Reviews, editorials, and studies focusing exclusively on older populations were excluded. Thirteen studies were identified, of which 7 met inclusion criteria. Of the 7 publications, some focused on infants or toddlers, whereas others provided extractable data for children aged ≤3 years. Across studies, symptom onset was reported as early as 7.5 months in 1 cohort. Probable RLS in infants and toddlers presents as a behavioral sleep disorder characterized by nocturnal motor restlessness, accompanied by sleep fragmentation and distress. A characteristic pattern of awakening after 1-3 hours of sleep with motor agitation was frequently described. Periodic limb movements and low ferritin levels provide supportive evidence. Iron supplementation has been associated with improvement in symptoms in select cohorts. Probable RLS can manifest as early as infancy, presenting as a behavioral phenotype. Increased awareness of early behavioral manifestations and consideration of iron status may facilitate earlier identification and management. Future studies are needed to develop diagnostic frameworks and to better define the natural history of early-onset probable RLS.

papers.title: The effect of climate on epigenetic changes in psychiatric disorders: an evolutionary perspective.
papers.abstract: There is increasing evidence that epigenetic mechanisms of gene expression are dysregulated in psychiatric disorders. Epigenetic mechanisms can be modified by environmental factors such as climate. Climate is also known to alter circadian rhythms. This review article examines the possible effects of climate on epigenetic mechanisms of gene expression in patients with common psychiatric disorders such as schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and major depressive disorder, from an evolutionary perspective. Implications for the mitigation of climate-induced mental illness are explored.

papers.title: A Novel Heterozygous KCNH2 c.1288G > C (p.A430P) Variant Causes Type 2 Long QT Syndrome Through Loss of hERG Channel Function.
papers.abstract: A novel variant in the KCNH2 gene (human ether-a-go-go-related gene, hERG) has been identified and is associated with type 2 long QT syndrome (LQT2). Integrating genotype analysis into clinical evaluation facilitates more accurate diagnosis and targeted therapeutic strategies for this condition. Sanger sequencing was used to detect the KCNH2 variant in an LQT2 family. The variant was transiently expressed in HEK293 cells for functional characterization via patch-clamp electrophysiology, Western blot, and qRT-PCR. A novel heterozygous missense variant KCNH2 c.1288G > C (p.Ala430Pro) was identified. Unlike wild-type (WT) channels, the A430P variant generated no detectable hERG currents. Western blot showed comparable protein expression between WT and A430P, both migrating at approximately 127 kDa, which corresponds to the core-glycosylated form. qRT-PCR revealed significantly elevated A430P mRNA levels compared to WT (p = 0.0027). The complete loss of channel function in the A430P variant is not due to reduced protein expression. The discordance between elevated mRNA and unchanged protein levels suggests post-transcriptional or translational dysregulation, expanding our understanding of LQT2 molecular mechanisms.

papers.title: A Biophysical Perspective on Microwave-Induced Neurobiological Effects.
papers.abstract: Microwave radiation interacts with the nervous system through a cascade of electromagnetic, thermal, and mechanical perturbations that drive a broad range of neurobiological responses. Although exposure guidelines are based on specific absorption rate (SAR), substantive evidence indicates that neurobiological effects arise across frequencies, waveforms, and SAR levels that SAR alone cannot characterize. We distinguish net-thermal, transient-thermal, and non-thermal mechanisms according to whether a response is mediated by the net temperature rise, by the heating rate and temperature gradients, or largerly independent of temperature change. This review traces the physical perturbation cascade from electromagnetic field distribution through thermal dynamics to thermoelastic stress, and reviews five biological endpoints: genotoxicity, molecular dysregulation and signaling, blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability, electrophysiology, and behavioral changes. A consistent finding is that many studies report associations with only SAR and frequency, omitting the intermediate physical quantities that drive the responses, and thus obscuring a mechanistic understanding of the causal chain. Mapping of reported studies into the SAR-frequency space reveals a clustering within the 0.9-3 GHz band and near SAR = 2 W/kg, with biological alterations reported below these limits under both continuous and pulsed exposures. These findings motivate future work that directly quantifies spatiotemporal physical perturbations to close the gap between exposure conditions and neurobiological outcomes.

papers.title: Bad Dreams and Eating Disorder-Related Impairment Among University Students.
papers.abstract: Sleep problems are elevated among people with eating disorder (ED) symptoms; however, there is little contemporary research on bad dreams and nightmares in this population. Students completed measures assessing ED-related impairment, sleep, depression, and anxiety. Ordinal logistic regressions were used to examine associations between ED-related impairment and bad dream frequency categories (i.e. past-month average of zero, <1/week, or ≥1/week). Greater eating disorder-related impairment was significantly associated with greater odds of having more frequent bad dreams, B = 0.61, SE = 0.08, OR = 1.84, 95% CI [1.59, 2.14], p < .001, after adjusting for gender and minoritized race/ethnicity. However, associations were smaller but still statistically significant after adjusting for depressive and anxiety symptoms, B = 0.23, SE = 0.10, OR = 1.26, 95% CI [1.04, 1.53], p = .02. Overall, findings suggest that greater ED-related impairment is associated with greater odds of having more frequent bad dreams. High frequency of bad dreams among those with ED-related impairment may be partially driven by comorbidity with other mental health conditions or general distress.

papers.title: SIRT7 Aggravates Chronic Sleep Deprivation-Induced Cognitive Impairment and Neuronal Apoptosis via Decreasing Succinylation and Cascaded Ubiquitylation of NFL.
papers.abstract: Insomnia affected one-third of the global population, but its molecular mechanism was not clarified. A chronic sleep deprivation (CSD) model was constructed in SD rats using multiple platforms over water. Hippocampal tissues were collected for ubiquitinomics and succinylomics. Sirtuin 7 (SIRT7) inhibitor was administered to elevate succinylation levels. Molecular experiments demonstrated the cascade reaction of succinylation and ubiquitylation, and Neurofilament Light (NFL)-binding ubiquitinating enzyme. Chronic sleep deprivation caused cognitive disorder of rats. Mostly, succinylation and ubiquitylation displayed a downregulated trend in the CSD group, especially double modification of NFL at K370 (succinylation site) and K267/281 (ubiquitylation site), whose protein level was upregulated in CSD rats. NFL was proved to be a target of SIRT7, a well-known desuccinylase. SIRT7 inhibitor weakened cognitive deficit, blocked neuronal apoptosis, decreased NFL expression, and increased succinylation and ubiquitylation levels, which were inverse in the CSD model and cells infected with SIRT7 overexpression adenovirus. SIRT7 suppressed not only succinylation but also ubiquitylation through K370 of NFL. Knockdown of NFL receded cognitive disorder and neuronal apoptosis. BRCA1 Associated Deubiquitinase 1 (BAP1) inhibited NFL ubiquitylation and subsequently degradation. SIRT7 inhibitor promoted succinylation and cascaded ubiquitylation, as well as disrupting the interaction between BAP1 and NFL, finally suppressing CSD.

papers.title: Dexmedetomidine Versus Propofol Induction for Sedated Radiologic Procedures in Patients With Trisomy 21.
papers.abstract: Patients with Trisomy 21 (T21) are more susceptible to sedation-related adverse events (AEs). Few studies address the risk of propofol or compare natural airway sedation regimens in this population. Dexmedetomidine (DEX) is less likely than propofol to result in AEs as it promotes a more natural sleep and less airway muscle relaxation. This study is a secondary analysis of prospectively collected data. We queried the Pediatric Sedation Research Consortium (PSRC) Database from the years 2020 to 2025. The demographic characteristics were summarized using descriptive statistics. The incidence of sedation-related AEs and sedation failures were described by induction drug (DEX vs. propofol). Any medication used other than DEX or propofol were excluded. We performed a propensity score analysis comparing the DEX cohort to the propofol cohort. All the statistical work was performed using SAS 9.4. A total of 337 patients met inclusion criteria. The average age was 7 years. Forty-four percent of AEs were partial airway obstruction. For the bivariate analyses, the AE outcome variable is statistically significant with the medication variable (χ2df=1=33.249, P<0.001). Induction with propofol had a 5 times higher odds of an AE (OR=5.069, 95% CI: 2.829-9.082). After propensity score matching, there are a total of 216 matched observations. In patients with T21 undergoing radiologic procedures, the odds of having any AE are higher with induction using propofol compared with DEX. Greater consideration should be given for use of DEX induction for patients with T21 undergoing sedated radiologic procedures.

papers.title: The Impact of Psychological Therapies on Well-Being and Quality of Life in Adult Chronic Migraine Patients: A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: Chronic migraine is defined as ≥ 15 headache days per month, with at least 8 days meeting the migraine criteria. It profoundly impairs quality of life and is often accompanied by comorbid insomnia and emotional distress. Despite growing interest in psychological and behavioral interventions in chronic pain, these approaches remain understudied in chronic migraine. To systematically review the impact of psychological and behavioral interventions on quality of life and well-being in adults with chronic migraine, and to compare intervention types across a range of clinical, psychological, and functional outcomes. A systematic search of electronic databases was conducted to identify studies evaluating psychological interventions for adults with chronic migraine. Titles and abstracts were screened, followed by full-text review against predefined eligibility criteria. Due to heterogeneity in interventions and outcomes, a narrative synthesis was undertaken. Four studies were included, examining mindfulness-based interventions and cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBTi) across outcomes for migraine disability, well-being, and frequency. Mindfulness-based approaches demonstrated significant reductions in headache frequency and disability, along with improved pain acceptance and mood. Intervention therapy showed rapid and marked benefits; mindfulness following medication withdrawal saw improvements in psychological well-being and migraine frequency up to 12 months post intervention; combining mindfulness with transcranial direct current simulation (tDCS) suggested additive benefits. CBTi showed significant improvements in sleep quality, with delayed but meaningful reductions in headache days. Emotional outcomes such as depressive symptoms improved modestly; anxiety was less consistently affected. Empirical research evaluating psychological therapies for chronic migraine with well-being and quality of life outcomes is notably limited. However, existing evidence shows promising benefits for adults with chronic migraine, improving aspects of physical, emotional, and functional well-being. Mindfulness appears particularly effective in reducing migraine burden, while CBTi addresses sleep-related pathways. These findings support integrating these modalities into holistic, patient-centered migraine care. A stepping stone into the future of migraine management which highlights the potential of psychological therapy successfully improving well-being and quality of life in migraine management.

papers.title: Morphological and Mechanical Properties of Masticatory Muscles in Individuals With Bruxism: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: Bruxism induces repetitive loading of the masticatory muscles, potentially causing structural and mechanical adaptations such as increased muscle thickness, stiffness and altered viscoelastic properties. However, findings across studies using ultrasonography, elastography and myotonometry remain inconsistent, and no comprehensive synthesis has integrated morphological and mechanical parameters across multiple muscles and modalities. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare the morphological and mechanical properties of masticatory muscles between individuals with and without bruxism. Following PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420261433530), Web of Science, PubMed and Scopus were searched for studies comparing masticatory muscle morphology and mechanical properties between bruxism patients and healthy controls. Two reviewers independently screened studies and assessed quality (Newcastle-Ottawa Scale). Random-effects meta-analyses (MD/SMD, 95% CI) were performed per muscle. Of 9 included studies, masseter muscle stiffness was significantly higher in bruxism patients (SMD, 1.87; 95% CI, 0.53-3.22; p = 0.006), while masseter and temporalis anterior muscle thickness showed no significant differences (p > 0.05). Diagnostic criteria strongly influenced thickness findings, with self-reported bruxism showing increased thickness and polysomnography-confirmed bruxism showing decreased thickness. Masseter muscle stiffness, but not thickness, is significantly altered in bruxism, suggesting mechanical properties may be a more sensitive and consistent indicator than gross morphology. PROSPERO, CRD420261433530.

papers.title: Which Lifestyle Is Associated With Frailty? Exploring Lifestyle Factors From Multiple Dimensions Among Rural Older Adults: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: To identify which indicators from multidimensional lifestyles are associated with frailty, to develop a lifestyle index and to explore the association between this index and frailty. A cross-sectional study with a multistage cluster random-sampling design. This study included 3279 rural older adults. The Fried frailty phenotype was used to assess frailty. Twenty-three lifestyle factors, including smoking, drinking, stationary time, exercise time, sleep time, nutrition indicators and social engagement, were evaluated. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression was used to select lifestyles associated with frailty and logistic regression with cluster-robust standard errors was employed to explore the associations between the lifestyle index and frailty and its subdomains. Restricted cubic spline analysis was performed to explore the dose-response relationship between lifestyle index and frailty. This study found that stationary time, exercise time, keeping up with political events and socializing with neighbours and friends were associated with frailty. After adjusting for covariates, the lifestyle index that included these four lifestyles was positively associated with frailty and with four subdomains including exhaustion, weakness, slowness and low physical activity, but was not associated with unintentional weight loss. There was no nonlinear relationship between frailty and the lifestyle index. Stationary time and exercise time were associated with frailty and its four dimensions. Additionally, social engagements were also significant factors associated with frailty, which highlights the importance of social networks in frailty. When delivering lifestyle health education related to frailty, nurses should prioritize the assessment of physical activity, stationary time and social engagement. Given the wide variety of lifestyles, targeted health education on lifestyle is of great significance for frailty management; it can also reduce nurses' workload and improve efficiency. This study adhered to the STROBE guidelines. No patient or public contribution.

papers.title: Neural Tracking of Continuous Speech Is Sensitive to Socially "Engaging" Prosodic Features of Conversational Anecdotes.
papers.abstract: While there is growing research on how the brain "entrains" to speech, it is unclear whether neural speech tracking is sensitive to interpersonally relevant changes in a speaker's tone of voice (prosody), such as when people try to sound "engaging" while telling conversational anecdotes. Here, we employed neural speech tracking to test whether listeners' speech encoding is enhanced by what a conversation is about and how speakers express themselves. Thirty-one participants listened to "gossip-like" anecdotes varying in topic (interesting vs. boring) and vocal delivery (engaging vs. neutral prosody) while recording their EEG. Participants estimated how long they would be willing to continue the interaction based on what they heard in each trial ("time bidding"). Neural speech tracking was quantified using Gaussian Copula Mutual Information between speech envelopes and EEG, and alpha power was analyzed as a complementary index of attentional engagement. Behaviorally, listeners preferred interesting (vs. boring) anecdotes and engaging (vs. neutral) sounding speakers; the effect of using an engaging prosody on time bids was stronger for interesting topics. At the neurophysiological level, engaging prosody enhanced neural speech tracking at frontal sites only when anecdotes were interesting, suggesting that neural encoding of social prosody depended on listeners' motivation to attend to the contents of speech. Alpha power displayed a distinct interaction over left-anterior sites, with opposite prosodic patterns for interesting and boring anecdotes; exploratory analyses suggested that lower left-anterior alpha power was associated with stronger neural speech tracking. Our study suggests that prosodic cues designed to engage a listener's attention enhance neural tracking of continuous speech, although these effects are constrained by broader contextual factors such as topic interest. These findings suggest that socially motivated vocal expression influences listeners' online neural encoding and highlight the importance of studying speech processing within its interpersonal communicative context.

papers.title: Best1 shapes the depth and stability of NREM sleep.
papers.abstract: Sleep architecture is orchestrated by neuronal circuits, yet the contribution of astrocytes-particularly to the depth and continuity of sleep-remains incompletely understood. Mammalian sleep is composed of rapid eye movement (REM) and non-REM (NREM) stages, with NREM further subdivided into light and deep phases. While neuronal and neurotransmitter-based mechanisms of sleep regulation have been extensively characterized, the role of astrocytic signaling in deep NREM sleep has received relatively little attention. Bestrophin-1 (Best1) is a calcium-activated anion channel highly enriched in astrocytes, known to mediate non-vesicular release of gliotransmitters such as glutamate, D-serine, and GABA, and to influence neuronal excitability. Here, we identify Best1 as a critical regulator of deep NREM sleep. Immunohistochemistry revealed robust Best1 expression in astrocytes across sleep-regulating brain regions. EEG/EMG polysomnography in Best1 knockout (Best1-KO) mice demonstrated a selective disruption of deep NREM sleep, despite preserved total sleep time and overall NREM duration. Best1-KO mice exhibited shorter deep NREM bouts, attenuated delta-band (0.5-4 Hz) EEG power, and altered vigilance-state transitions, with reduced entry into and maintenance of deep NREM. Sleep trajectories were biased toward Wake → light NREM → REM transitions, frequently bypassing deep sleep stages. Spectral decomposition further confirmed diminished delta oscillations during NREM episodes. These findings establish Best1 as a substage-specific molecular gatekeeper of deep NREM sleep. By uncovering a glial mechanism that shapes sleep sub-architecture, this work highlights astrocytic ion signaling as a promising therapeutic target for disorders marked by fragmented or insufficient deep sleep, including those associated with aging and neurodegenerative disease.

papers.title: Distinct trajectories of 24-hour sleep duration and subsequent functional limitations in older adults: a national longitudinal cohort study.
papers.abstract: Static sleep duration is a known health determinant, yet the prognostic value of longitudinal 24-hour sleep trajectories for functional deterioration remains understudied. However, whether longitudinal 24-hour sleep trajectories are associated with subsequent overall and severe functional limitations remains unclear. We analysed 4,999 adults aged ≥ 50 years from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), free of baseline functional limitations. Latent class mixed models identified distinct 24-hour sleep duration trajectories over 4 years. We estimated risk ratios (RRs) for ADL and IADL limitations at Wave 5, as well as severe limitations defined as difficulty in two or more tasks. Three trajectories were identified: Stable Moderate (56.5%), Progressively Short (13.5%; ~5.1 h to ~ 3.9 h), and Progressively Long (30.0%; ~8.4 h to ~ 9.2 h). Compared with the Stable Moderate group, the Progressively Short trajectory was associated with higher risks of ADL limitation (RR = 1.34; 95% CI: 1.18-1.52) and IADL limitation (RR = 1.22; 95% CI: 1.08-1.37) at Wave 5, as well as severe ADL limitation. Conversely, the Progressively Long trajectory was not associated with overall ADL or IADL limitations at Wave 5, but was associated with severe ADL and IADL limitations. Longitudinal changes in 24-hour sleep duration were associated with subsequent functional limitations in older adults. Progressively sleep shortening may serve as a marker of functional vulnerability, whereas sleep lengthening may indicate more advanced dependency. These findings support the potential value of sleep trajectories for risk stratification, while causal interpretation requires caution.

papers.title: The endothelial PECAM1-CXCR4 axis amplifies neutrophil degranulation to exacerbate sleep-deprived periodontitis: a systems-level framework for comorbidity therapy.
papers.abstract: Sleep deprivation (SD), a global public health issue, induces systemic low-grade inflammation and vascular endothelial dysfunction, and is a confirmed risk factor for periodontitis (PD). PD is driven by vascular-immune imbalance and excessive neutrophil activation/degranulation, yet the molecular mechanism linking SD-induced systemic changes to local periodontal inflammation remains unclear, leaving a lack of precise therapeutic targets for SD-PD comorbidity. Here, we conducted a systems-level study integrating population epidemiology (NHANES/KNHANES), clinical sample validation, multi-omics bioinformatics analysis, and in vitro/in vivo models. We screened SD-PD core hub genes via WGCNA, DEG and disease target mining, elucidated their regulatory role in neutrophil degranulation with cellular models, and identified candidate dual-target agents by molecular docking/MDS, then validated the candidate drug's efficacy in SD-PD comorbidity mice with multiple detection techniques. We first confirmed in human cohorts and mouse models that SD exacerbates neutrophil-mediated periodontal bone loss. Integrative bioinformatic analysis pinpointed endothelial PECAM1 and neutrophil CXCR4 as key molecules. Mechanistically, we reveal that under inflammatory conditions, endothelial PECAM1 can physically interact with CXCL12, potentially acting as a molecular sink that influences its local availability. This ligand scarcity triggers a compensatory upregulation of its receptor, CXCR4, on neutrophils. Consequently, these primed neutrophils become hyper-reactive, leading to excessive degranulation and tissue destruction upon stimulation. Leveraging this mechanism, we computationally identified and experimentally validated curcumin as a dual-functional modulator of PECAM1 and CXCR4. In our comorbidity mouse model, curcumin not only blocked this pathological axis to mitigate periodontal destruction but also associated with partial recovery of NREM sleep architecture, possibly through mitigation of systemic inflammation. Our findings establish the PECAM1-CXCR4 axis as a critical, druggable pathway in sleep-inflammation comorbidity and provide a conceptual framework for treating complex systemic-local disorders.

papers.title: The hidden burden of insomnia in late pregnancy: prevalence and risk factors among Egyptian women.
papers.abstract: Insomnia is a prevalent sleep condition that has a harmful impact on one's quality of life and presents considerable health hazards, especially for pregnant women in their third trimester. It can lead to stress, postpartum depression and negative fetal outcomes. The prevalence and contributing variables of insomnia among pregnant women in Egypt have not been adequately studied. This study evaluated the prevalence of insomnia among third trimester pregnant women in Egypt and analyzed the associated risk factors. This is a cross-sectional study of pregnant women in the third trimester at Menoufia University Hospital. The study included 390 participants. The study employed a pre-structured questionnaire that includes questions about sociodemographic and lifestyle attributes, accompanied by the ISI questionnaire used to diagnose and assess insomnia severity. A total of 390 pregnant women in the third trimester completed the questionnaire. The prevalence of insomnia was 75.4% (n = 294), with 33.1% categorized as sub-threshold, 26.2% as moderate, and 16.2% as severe. Multivariate logistic regression identified maternal age 25-35 years (AOR = 4.57, 95% CI: 2.50-8.36) and age > 35 years (AOR = 3.27, 95% CI: 1.01-9.70) as significant risk factors. Conversely, university education (AOR = 0.26, 95% CI: 0.11-0.61), overweight BMI (AOR = 0.32, 95% CI: 0.16-0.62), and rural residence (AOR = 0.53, 95% CI: 0.30-0.95) were significant protective factors. Linear regression further confirmed that higher insomnia severity scores were predicted by increased maternal age, while overweight BMI (B = -3.10), rural residence (B = -1.98), and nulliparity (B = -3.69) were significant negative predictors of severity (p < 0.05). Insomnia is highly prevalent among pregnant women, particularly in the third trimester. Advanced maternal age and urban residence were associated with a higher risk and severity of insomnia, while higher education and nulliparity appear protective. Further research is needed to develop strategies to improve maternal well-being and reduce adverse outcomes for mothers and infants.

papers.title: Associations of sleep architecture, sleep fragmentation, and hypoxia-related parameters with cognitive frailty in older patients with hypertension and obstructive sleep apnea: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: To investigate the associations of sleep architecture, sleep fragmentation, and nocturnal hypoxia-related parameters with cognitive frailty (CF) in older patients with hypertension and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). In this single-center cross-sectional study, 240 hospitalized patients aged ≥ 60 years with hypertension and OSA confirmed by polysomnography (PSG) were enrolled between January 2025 and January 2026. Participants were classified into a CF group (n = 83) and a non-CF group (n = 157). Demographic and clinical data were collected. Cognitive frailty was assessed using the Chinese version of the Montreal Cognitive Assessment and the Fried Frailty Phenotype. PSG variables included total sleep time, sleep-stage durations, arousal index, apnea-hypopnea index, oxygen desaturation index, minimum oxygen saturation, and mean oxygen saturation. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with CF. Compared with the non-CF group, the CF group had shorter N3 sleep duration, lower minimum oxygen saturation, and a higher arousal index. After adjustment for sex, age, years of education, and body mass index, N3 sleep duration (OR = 0.988, 95% CI: 0.981-0.996, P = 0.002) and minimum oxygen saturation (OR = 0.945, 95% CI: 0.914-0.977, P < 0.001) were independently negatively associated with CF, whereas arousal index (OR = 1.016, 95% CI: 1.005-1.027, P = 0.005) was independently positively associated with CF. Age was also independently associated with CF. Reduced N3 sleep duration, lower minimum oxygen saturation, and higher arousal index were associated with CF in older patients with hypertension and OSA, supporting the need for prospective studies to clarify temporal relationships.

papers.title: Longitudinal exploration of auditory sensory-perceptual processing in CLN3 disease (Juvenile Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis (Batten disease)): A high-density auditory evoked potential (AEP) study.
papers.abstract: There is currently limited information about sensory and perceptual abilities across the progression of CLN3 disease (Juvenile Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis; Batten disease), a recessively inherited lysosomal storage disorder and a leading cause of childhood neurodegeneration. Clinical symptoms include vision loss, motor impairments, and cognitive challenges, making it difficult to accurately assess neurocognitive and perceptual abilities. Thus, there is a critical need to identify objective biomarkers that can be used to inform disease progression and track treatment response in this population. This exploratory case series investigates longitudinal changes in auditory sensory perceptual processing over several years in a small sample of individuals with genetically confirmed CLN3 disease (N = 4; 3 male) compared to a cross-sectional sample of 60 neurotypical (NT) controls using high-density electroencephalography (EEG). We utilized a duration mismatch negativity (MMN) paradigm, identical to what has been used in our previous cross-sectional study. We examined the auditory evoked potentials (AEPs) of the standard tones across three different stimulus onset asynchrony conditions and examined the N1 and P2 components of the AEP. Early evidence shows differences in the amplitudes of the N1 and P2 components in individuals with CLN3 disease relative to NT controls. These amplitude differences were most notable in CLN3 disease when participants were presented with standard tones that had the slowest presentation rate. Specifically, N1 and P2 amplitudes were more negative than NT controls in childhood and adolescence and as CLN3 disease participants aged, the amplitude of the AEPs was more positive than controls. Further, a more positive N1 amplitude during the longest stimulus presentation condition was associated with both reduced verbal intelligence and working memory abilities in CLN3 disease participants. Our preliminary case-series findings parallel recently published work in a mouse model of CLN3 disease that showed both sex- and age-dependent disruptions in central auditory processing. Taken together, we demonstrate the utility of auditory EEG measures as a sensitive, objective and translational measure in CLN3 disease that may serve as a potential outcome measure useful in tracking disease progression. Continued work is needed in humans focused on sex-based differences and longitudinal changes of auditory processing in CLN3 disease.

papers.title: Mismatched findings on ancillary examinations in virus-associated acute encephalopathy and encephalitis: pathological mechanisms and clinical significance.
papers.abstract: In this review, we group three mechanistically distinct categories of acute brain dysfunction after viral infection under the term "virus-associated acute encephalopathy and encephalitis": (1) viral encephalitis, caused by direct invasion and replication of neurotropic viruses in the central nervous system; (2) post-infectious autoimmune encephalitis, triggered by infection-induced central nervous system autoimmune responses; and (3) acute encephalopathy syndromes without direct central nervous system infection, resulting from systemic inflammatory storms or hypoxia. The three entities are grouped as a conceptual framework rather than an established classification because they all present as acute brain dysfunction occurring in association with viral infection and differ only in mechanism. The diagnosis of virus-associated acute encephalopathy and encephalitis relies mainly on ancillary examinations, including neuroimaging, cerebrospinal fluid analysis, and electroencephalography. In clinical practice, ancillary findings are frequently mismatched: some tests may be negative while others are positive, and results can evolve with the pathological mechanism and disease stage. Recognizing these mismatches can help clinicians identify the possible mechanism of central nervous system injury and avoid diagnostic and treatment delays, and guide further testing. In particular, empirical intravenous acyclovir should be started promptly when herpes simplex virus (HSV) or varicella-zoster virus (VZV) encephalitis is clinically suspected. This article reviews the mechanisms of virus-associated acute encephalopathy and encephalitis, and discusses the common causes of such mismatches and strategies to manage them; the proposed framework is hypothesis-generating and is not intended as a validated diagnostic algorithm.

papers.title: Modulation of cell to cell action potential conduction by the dynamic clamp: gap junction and ephaptic coupling.
papers.abstract: Cardiac conduction is primarily attributed to gap junctions (GJs), although ephaptic mechanisms involving Na⁺ channels (Nav1.5) in the intercalated disc (ID) have been suggested to contribute to action potential (AP) conduction when GJ coupling is reduced. We used a two-cell preparation combined with dynamic clamp to experimentally modulate cell-to-cell AP transmission by varying gap junction conductacleft across the two disc membranesnce (gj). In passive HEK293 cells expressing connexin 43 (Cx43) and Nav1.5, APs were generated by injecting computer-simulated inward rectifier (IK1) and pacemaker (If) currents via patch pipettes under current-clamp conditions. Three experimental configurations were examined: (1) physically GJ-coupled pairs (cells connected by actual Cx43 channels); (2) virtually coupled pairs (no physical GJ connection; coupling imposed in real time by dynamic clamp); and (3) physically GJ-coupled pairs rendered virtually uncoupled (physical GJ connection computationally negated by dynamic clamp, while physically preserving ID-like architecture). Intercellular AP conduction delay (Δt) was measured in physically and virtually coupled cell pairs. In all configurations, Δt increased nonlinearly as gj decreased, with conduction failure occurring below ~ 1 nS in the absence of ephaptic contributions. Ephaptic transmission was observed in Cx43 knockout HEK293/Nav1.5 cells and GJ-coupled HEK293/Nav1.5 pairs in which gj was computationally negated via dynamic clamp. In both cases, AP conduction persisted even when gj was eliminated entirely or reduced below 1 nS. A structurally based mathematical model of the intercalated disc accurately predicted the voltage response of ephaptically activated current in the recipient cell. Together, these data provide direct experimental evidence of ephaptic coupling in closely apposed cell pairs and demonstrate that, in a cardiac-analogue HEK293 system, ephaptic mechanisms can sustain AP conduction when GJ conductance is reduced or absent.
papers.journal: Pflugers Archiv : European journal of physiology

papers.title: Multidimensional sleep-wake changes and risk of all-cause and cardiovascular disease mortality in oldest-old women.
papers.abstract: Sleep-wake patterns often worsen with age and are fundamental to health, yet little is known about their long-term changes in the oldest old and links to mortality risk. We aimed to characterize five-year changes in 24-hour sleep-wake patterns and examine associations with all-cause and cardiovascular disease mortality among community-dwelling women in their 80s and 90s. Among 704 community-dwelling older women (mean age 82.9 years at baseline), we objectively measured 24-hour sleep-wake parameters-including nighttime sleep, daytime napping, and circadian rest-activity rhythms-using 4-night/5-day actigraphy at baseline and again five years later. We used hierarchical clustering on principal components analysis to identify profiles of sleep-wake changes and used Cox proportional hazards models to assess associations with mortality. Here we show that compared to those with stable patterns, women experiencing declining nighttime sleep (hazard ratio [HR] = 2.16 [95% CI: 1.26, 3.72]) or increasing 24-hour sleepiness (HR = 2.09 [1.12, 3.92]) have approximately double the risk of subsequent all-cause mortality over a median follow-up time of 2.1 years, independent of comorbidities and covariates. We also find that increases in daytime napping duration are associated with over double the risk of all-cause (HR = 2.24 [1.25, 4.01]) and cardiovascular disease mortality (HR = 2.93 [1.14, 7.51]), while decreases in nighttime sleep duration are linked to elevated cardiovascular disease mortality (HR = 2.78 [1.06, 7.31]). Our findings suggest that changes in 24-hour sleep/circadian patterns among the oldest old are not simply normal aging but may serve as an important marker of increased mortality risk.

papers.title: Low carbohydrate high fat diet curbs glioblastoma by shifting lipids and limiting cancer stem cell metabolic flexibility.
papers.abstract: Metabolic rewiring fuels tumorigenicity of cancer stem cells contributing to universal glioblastoma (GBM) recurrence. Invasive glioblastoma stem cells (GSCs), already unresectable, acquire tumorigenic properties that confer therapy resistance. Using samples from both recurrent and newly diagnosed GBM patients, we identified fatty acid oxidation (FAO) as a key pathway supporting GSC tumorigenicity. Transcriptomic profiling, compared against non-malignant human astrocytes from epilepsy patients, highlighted an FAO-enriched signature in GSCs. In vivo studies showed that tumor formation by these GSCs could be modulated by altering the availability of metabolizable lipids in the brain, with beneficial effects observed under a low carbohydrate high fat diet (LCHFD). The lipid metabolism contributing to GSC mediated tumor formation was confirmed using metabolomic and lipidomic analyses. Gut microbiome analyses revealed that LCHFD shapes the microbiome and modulates the circadian network. By targeting FAO in the postoperative period before chemoradiation, LCHFD offers a non-pharmacologic strategy to delay GBM recurrence. This study suggests a mechanistic framework for dietary modulation as a therapeutic approach to improve GBM outcomes.

papers.title: MyoGen: unified biophysical modeling of human neuromotor activity and resulting signals.
papers.abstract: Understanding human motor control requires integrating cortical and spinal activity, muscle mechanics, and electrophysiology, which are typically studied in isolation. We present MyoGen, an open-source framework that unifies spinal circuitry, proprioceptive feedback, musculotendon dynamics, and multimodal electromyography generation. Using data-driven optimization benchmarked against human motor unit recordings, MyoGen produces motor unit population activity matching experimental discharge-rate distributions and variability across muscles. The framework generates decomposable surface and intramuscular electromyography, reproduces beta-band modulation of descending drive and its transformation into force, and implements key sensorimotor loop components. Dimensionality reduction of simulated agonist-antagonist electromyography reveals low-dimensional control manifolds consistent with recordings from able-bodied individuals and those with spinal cord injury. Here, we show that MyoGen provides a physiologically grounded simulation substrate, enabling systematic investigation of motor control principles, benchmarking of signal-processing algorithms, and exploration of experimentally inaccessible sensorimotor interactions.

papers.title: Lesions of anterior cingulate cortex disrupt an electrophysiological signature of goal completion in humans.
papers.abstract: The reward positivity (RewP) is an event-related brain potential (ERP) component associated with feedback and goal completion. Although the component is said to be generated in anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), this inference is disputed because of the inverse problem. Recent intracranial electroencephalogram (EEG) current source density analyses provided direct evidence that the RewP is generated in caudal ACC, specifically Brodmann areas 24c' and 32'. To further test this hypothesis, we examined the effects of damage to frontal cortex damage on RewP amplitude. Scalp EEG was recorded from 68 stroke patients with frontal lesions while they performed a trial-and-error guessing task used to elicit a canonical RewP. Non-parametric voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping revealed that damage to Brodmann areas 24c' and 32' significantly attenuated RewP amplitude. These results align with evidence suggesting a single generator of the RewP in the caudal ACC, supporting the role of caudal ACC in motivation of extended behaviors.

papers.title: [Development of an optimal acupuncture-moxibustion treatment protocol for perimenopausal insomnia].
papers.abstract: To systematically evaluate various acupuncture-moxibustion treatment regimens for perimenopausal insomnia using network meta-analysis combined with multi-criteria decision making (MCDM) approach, and to identify interventions with optimal overall efficacy across multiple dimensions, so as to provide a scientific basis for clinical decision-making. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) on acupuncture-moxibustion treatment for perimenopausal insomnia published from database inception to September 27, 2025 were systematically searched in the China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), VIP Chinese Journal Service Platform (VIP), Wanfang Data Knowledge Service Platform, China Biology Medicine Database (SinoMed), PubMed, EMbase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science. Network meta-analysis was performed using R software (version 4.4.3), and surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) value was calculated. A multidimensional evaluation system was established using the total effective rate, Pittsburgh sleep quality index (PSQI) score, and modified Kupperman menopausal index (KMI) score as efficacy indexes, and treatment frequency as the cost index. The entropy weight method was applied to determine index weight, and the weighted normalized decision matrix was analyzed using technique for order preference by similarity to ideal solution (TOPSIS) and multi-criteria optimization and compromise solution (Vlsekriterijumska Optimizacija I Kompromisno Resenje, VIKOR), two methods of MCDM, to comprehensively rank different acupuncture-moxibustion related interventions. A total of 32 RCTs were finally eligible, involving 19 acupuncture-moxibustion related protocols and 3 control measures. Network meta-analysis showed: for the total effective rate, the cumulative ranking curve was high for depression-relieving acupuncture therapy combined with western medication (SUCRA = 0.76), mind-regulating acupuncture therapy combined with Chinese herbal medication (SUCRA=0.75), and acupuncture at back-shu points of five zang organs combined with warming needle (SUCRA=0.75); for improvement in PSQI scores, cumulative ranking curve was high for abdominal acupuncture combined with Chinese herbal medication (SUCRA=0.93), depression-relieving acupuncture therapy combined with western medication (SUCRA=0.93), and acupuncture at back-shu points of five zang organs combined with warming needle (SUCRA= 0.84); and for improvement in modified KMI scores, it was high for warm needling (SUCRA=0.95), time-based acupoint selection acupuncture (SUCRA=0.79), and scalp acupuncture (SUCRA=0.76). MCDM analysis on treatment frequency demonstrated that acupuncture at back-shu points of five zang organs combined with warming needle ranked first in both TOPSIS and VIKOR methods, with relative closeness of 0.780 8 and Q value of 0, respectively. Acupuncture at back-shu points of five zang organs combined with warming needle demonstrates the advantages in both efficacy and cost, showing superior comprehensive performance among various acupuncture-moxibustion related interventions for perimenopausal insomnia, and it may serve as a clinically recommended option.
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion

papers.title: [Clinical efficacy of fire needle therapy for obstructive sleep apnea hypopnea syndrome based on a single-arm objective performance criterion design].
papers.abstract: To observe the clinical efficacy of fire needle therapy for obstructive sleep apnea hypopnea syndrome (OSAHS) using a single-arm objective performance criterion design. Forty patients with OSAHS were recruited, with 1 case dropped out and 3 cases were eliminated. On the basis of health education, patients received fire needle treatment at Baihui (GV20), Lianquan (CV23), and bilateral Lieque (LU7), Fenglong (ST40), Zhaohai (KI6), and Sanyinjiao (SP6), twice weekly for 4 consecutive weeks. The apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), oxygen desaturation index (ODI), longest apnea duration, mean oxygen saturation (MSpO2) during sleep, lowest oxygen saturation (LSpO2) during sleep, percentage of total sleep time with pulse oxygen saturation <90% (T-SpO2<90%), Epworth sleepiness scale (ESS) score, Pittsburgh sleep quality index (PSQI) score, and traditional Chinese medicine syndrome score were observed before and after treatment. The Vancouver scar scale (VSS) was used to evaluate the safety of fire needle treatment. The effective rate of continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) was used as the objective performance criterion, and clinical efficacy was evaluated after treatment. After treatment, AHI, ODI, longest apnea duration, T-SpO2<90%, ESS score, PSQI score, and traditional Chinese medicine syndrome score were lower than those before treatment (P<0.05), whereas MSpO2 and LSpO2 during sleep were higher than those before treatment (P<0.05). The total effective rate was 72.2% (26/36), with the lower limit of the one-sided confidence interval being 55%, which was higher than the objective performance criterion of 53.6%. The VSS score was (0.50±0.73) points, indicating good safety. Fire needle therapy can reduce the severity of snoring in patients with OSAHS, improve daytime sleepiness and nighttime sleep quality, increase oxygen saturation during nighttime sleep, and reduce traditional Chinese medicine syndrome score, with good safety.

papers.title: Critical methodological vulnerabilities, data discrepancies, and mechanistic paradoxes in evaluating repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation combined with Tai Chi for mild cognitive impairment.
papers.abstract: This correspondence provides a critical methodological and statistical re-appraisal of the recent clinical trial by Bai et al. (2026) [1], which investigated the combination of Yang-style Tai Chi and neuronavigated 1-Hz repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) for older adults with mild cognitive impairment and co-occurring sleep disorders. While evaluating non-pharmacological multimodal interventions in psychogeriatric populations represents a vital scientific pursuit, our in-depth evaluation reveals substantial vulnerabilities that undermine the trial's confirmatory conclusions. First, improper post-randomization exclusions of baseline-ineligible individuals resulted in an attrition rate exceeding 32%, fundamentally violating the intention-to-treat principle. Second, Table 1 displays critical computational discrepancies, including missing participant counts, impossible non-integer frequencies, and mathematically implausible test statistics (x² and P-values). Third, reliance on raw change-score analyses rather than baseline-adjusted ANCOVA leaves the behavioral findings vulnerable to Lord's paradox and regression to the mean. Fourth, the neuroimaging findings present a mechanistic paradox-wherein functional connectivity gains in the sham arm significantly exceeded those in the active group-compounded by non-independent seed selection ("double dipping"). Finally, the twice-daily high-density regimen incurs feasibility challenges, while evening inhibitory rTMS introduces chronobiological inconsistencies lacking objective sleep verification. We urge the authors to clarify these data discrepancies and recommend that the proposed synergistic effects be interpreted with caution.

papers.title: Electroencephalography-derived spectral edge frequency 95 targets in toddlers under propofol anaesthesia✰.
papers.abstract: Proprietary processed EEG indices are less accurate in young children. We evaluated spectral edge frequency 95 (SEF95), a nonproprietary EEG index representing the frequency below which 95% of total EEG power resides, to establish target thresholds for varying anaesthetic depths during propofol anaesthesia in toddlers. Secondary objectives were to assess the relationship between SEF95 and plasma propofol concentration, and to evaluate airway reactivity during laryngoscopy. In this prospective study of toddlers aged 13 to 24 months, Dixon's up-and-down method and centred isotonic regression were used to determine the SEF95 targets for 50% (ED50) and 90% (ED90) probability of nonresponse to three clinical stimuli: pacifier placement (assessing consciousness), electrical nerve stimulation (nociception), and laryngoscopy (intubation readiness). Linear mixed-effects regression was used to analyse the association between plasma propofol concentration and SEF95. Among 51 toddlers, SEF95 ED50 and ED90 targets (Hz) were 21.8 (90% CI 20.8-23.4) and 20.3 (19.1-20.7) Hz for pacifier placement, 12.0 (10.8-18.3) and 10.4 (8.7-11.3) Hz for electrical stimulation, and 10.3 (4.6-11.8) and 4.4 (1.5-5.4) Hz for laryngoscopy. Each 1 Hz increase in SEF95 corresponded to a 0.21 μg ml-1 decrease in plasma propofol (r=0.46, P<0.001), as described by the equation: plasma propofol concentration (μg ml-1)=5.80-0.21×SEF95 (Hz). This study defined EEG SEF95 targets for loss of consciousness, response to noxious stimuli, and intubation readiness in toddlers aged 13 to 24 months. When combined with existing infant data, these age-specific SEF95 targets can optimise propofol titration and dosing accuracy during EEG-guided propofol anaesthesia in patients aged <2 yr. NCT05701748. Registered 17 January 2023; PI: Ian Yuan.

papers.title: Short sleep for whom? Toward a personalized definition of sleep duration adequacy.
Coincidence detection in aspiny interneuron dendrites.
papers.abstract: Recent evidence for long-term potentiation (LTP) at glutamatergic synapses on GABAergic interneurons calls for close attention to the sub-cellular phenomena that underlie the induction of plasticity in aspiny dendrites. Neurogliaform interneurons exhibit large NMDA receptor-mediated currents, Hebbian LTP and supralinear summation of glutamatergic signals converging on dendritic compartments. Dendritic supralinearity in interneurons does not require sodium channels. Here we investigate the principles governing supralinear synaptic integration and its interaction with backpropagating action potentials in the synaptic plasticity context. We developed a biophysically realistic, multi-compartmental model of a murine (Mus musculus, male and female) hippocampal neurogliaform interneuron, with dendritic architecture and ion channel densities tuned to match ex vivo recordings. The interaction between synaptic inputs and action potentials was tested with patch-clamp electrophysiology and two-photon imaging of dendritic calcium-dependent fluorescence transients. Whether simulated glutamatergic excitatory postsynaptic potentials are clustered on a dendritic fragment or dispersed across the entire arbor, they summate supralinearly as assessed from the calculated somatic voltage response. Clustered inputs induce more pronounced local depolarizations and calcium transients than dispersed inputs. Action potentials generated at the soma backpropagate throughout the dendritic arbor but are attenuated at branch points. Coincident synaptic input and backpropagating action potentials relieve this attenuation, further enhance dendritic depolarizations, and greatly potentiate calcium influx via NMDA receptors. Despite differences in dendritic anatomy and in the roles of sodium channels, the interplay of orthodromic and antidromic voltage propagation and resultant calcium signal amplification exhibits remarkable similarities between neurogliaform interneurons and principal cells.Significance Statement Neurogliaform interneurons are key regulators of brain circuit activity, yet the dendritic mechanisms that enable these inhibitory cells to undergo synaptic plasticity remain poorly understood. Combining biophysically realistic computer modeling with electrophysiology and two-photon calcium imaging, we show that coincident synaptic input and backpropagating action potentials strongly amplify dendritic depolarization and calcium influx in these interneurons. Although their dendrites lack spines and do not rely on sodium-channel-dependent dendritic spikes, neurogliaform interneurons nonetheless use computational principles remarkably similar to those of excitatory principal neurons. These findings advance the understanding of how inhibitory circuits support learning-related plasticity and may provide foundational insight into disorders such as epilepsy and schizophrenia, in which abnormal dendritic signalling and inhibitory dysfunction are implicated.

papers.title: Speech and Language Abnormalities in Putative Brain-First Versus Body-First Parkinson's Disease.
papers.abstract: The α-synuclein origin model proposes brain-first and body-first Parkinson's disease (PD) subtypes, with speech potentially revealing their distinct neurodegenerative patterns. We aimed to analyze the possible speech and language differences between untreated PD patients with premotor (putative body-first) and without (putative brain-first) rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder. Speech samples of reading passages and monologues were automatically analyzed using acoustic and linguistic features. We enrolled 23 body-first and 35 brain-first de novo PD patients compared with 35 healthy controls. Brain-first patients showed greater speech impairment severity compared with body-first patients (P = 0.002) and controls (P < 0.001), whereas body-first patients showed greater language impairment severity compared with brain-first patients (P < 0.001) and controls (P < 0.001). Putative brain-first subtype had more motor speech abnormalities whereas body-first subtype manifested greater language impairment. Thes finding is consistent with motor-dominant nigrostriatal involvement in brain-first and broader non-motor/cognitive involvement in body-first PD. © 2026 The Author(s).
