papers.title: Neuroscience-informed psychoeducation for bipolar disorder.
papers.abstract: Neuroscience-informed psychoeducation (NIPE) extends traditional psychoeducation for bipolar disorder by grounding clinical content in the neural mechanisms underlying the illness. This chapter reviews the neuroscience foundation relevant to bipolar disorder, including prefrontal-limbic circuit dysfunction, reward processing abnormalities that shift between mood states, circadian rhythm disruption, autonomic dysregulation, and the neuroplastic changes linked to illness progression and recovery. We translate these mechanisms into accessible psychoeducational content addressing diagnosis, pathogenesis, risk factors, and treatment, and describe brain-based strategies spanning cognitive monitoring, circadian-focused interventions, and emerging digital phenotyping tools. Delivery considerations are addressed with attention to the state-dependent nature of insight and cognitive function across mood episodes, phenotype-specific personalization, and family involvement. We outline mechanisms through which NIPE may improve outcomes, including enhanced awareness, reduced stigma, improved treatment adherence, and greater self-efficacy. While empirical evaluation of NIPE specifically for bipolar disorder remains limited, the chapter identifies priorities for future research, including randomized trials, mechanistic mediation analyses, and precision medicine approaches tailored to bipolar phenotype and illness course.

papers.title: Structural characterization and immunostimulatory activity comparison of two galactofucans from Undaria pinnatifida Sporophyll.
papers.abstract: Two highly sulfated galactofucans were isolated from the sporophylls of Undaria pinnatifida, and their structures were elucidated by methylation analysis, FTIR and NMR spectral analysis, together with HPLC, HPGPC and LXQ (ESI-MS). Comparison of the two U. pinnatifida sporophyll galactofucans (UPSG1 and UPSG2) revealed that UPSG1 exhibited a lower molecular weight than UPSG2 and that O-acetyl groups were present only in UPSG1. Meanwhile, both UPSG1 and UPSG2 possessed a backbone composed of →3)-⍺-L-Fucp4S-(1→, →3,4)-β-D-Galp-(1→, and →3)-β-D-Galp4S-(1 → residues. Moreover, they both showed immunostimulatory activities. Notably, UPSG1 exhibited stronger immunostimulatory activity than UPSG2, as evidenced by its greater capacity to promote NO production and the secretion of TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β, as well as the expression of the M1 marker CD86 in macrophages. In addition, UPSG1 and UPSG2 upregulated the expression of NF-κB, NLRP3, and Caspase-1 proteins, which are involved in inflammatory signaling. The present study elucidates the structure and immunomodulatory activity of U. pinnatifida sporophylls galactofucans, thereby providing a theoretical basis for the utilization of sporophylls, a processing by-product of U. pinnatifida.

papers.title: Sleep and Orofacial Pain.
papers.abstract: Sleep disorders and some orofacial pain disorders, such as temporomandibular disorders and headaches, have a bidirectional relationship: a sleep disturbance can worsen pain, and pain can interfere with sleep. Clinicians who manage orofacial pain need to be aware of this important relationship and screen their patients for a possible sleep disorder, especially insomnia, obstructive sleep apnea, and sleep bruxism. This article also discusses the influence of disturbed sleep on headaches and musculoskeletal pain, and the effect of commonly used medications for orofacial pain on sleep.

papers.title: Evaluation of the Orofacial Pain Patient.
papers.abstract: An orofacial pain evaluation consists of 4 parts. The first and most important is the patient history, which is a largely verbal review of the patient's chief complaints, history of present illness, past medical and dental history, review of systems, psychosocial history, and sleep history. Second, the physical examination determines the source of pain and any dysfunction in the masticatory system and includes cranial nerve screening, head and neck range of motion assessments, and muscle and joint palpations. Third, diagnostic tests, such as anesthetic blocks, may indicate the source of pain. Finally, laboratory tests may be indicated.

papers.title: [Characteristics of Patients with Digital Health Applications for Mental Disorders - Analysis results of insured persons in Rhineland Palatinate/Saarland].
papers.abstract: Insured patients with a prescription for a digital health application for mental disorders (PsyDiGA) receive an activation code from their health insurance. We examined characteristics of insured persons receiving and redeeming an activation code. Billing data of insured adults with mental disorders from AOK Rhineland-Palatinate and Saarland in 2020-2022 were analysed using logistic regression models. The sample for the analysis comprised 280,706 insured persons: 280,103 insured persons without an activation code and 603 insured persons with one (of whom 457 had redeemed theirs). Female patients, patients younger than 35 years as well as those with depressive, anxiety or sleep disorders were more likely to receive an activation code (e. g. odds ratio (OR) female vs. male 1.32, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.12-1.57; depressive vs. other disorder adjusted OR 2.36 (95% CI 1.94-2.89)). Patients aged 35-44 years were less likely to redeem an activation code compared to those aged 25-34 years (OR 0.46, 95%-CI 0.27-0.78). Our PsyDiGA results based on data from the AOK align with other insurance companies reporting that DiGA are prescribed primarily to women and younger people. Before prescribing a PsyDiGA in case of a suitable indication, especially to persons aged 35-44 years, physicians and psychotherapists should discuss with their patients whether PsyDiGA can be integrated into their daily routine.

papers.title: Sleep apnea is associated with glucose intolerance and presenteeism even in mild, asymptomatic, and non-obese cases: a cross-sectional study of Japanese workers.
papers.abstract: We examined the prevalence of mild sleep apnea syndrome (SAS) among Japanese workers, its associations with glucose intolerance and work productivity, and how well conventional screening parameters identify it. In this cross-sectional study at a medical foundation hospital in Tokyo, Japan (December 2023-February 2024), 71 employees (17 men, 54 women) underwent home sleep apnea testing to derive the respiratory event index (REI). We also used annual health checkup data, the Japanese Epworth Sleepiness Scale (JESS), the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI-J), and the WHO Health and Work Performance Questionnaire. Glucose intolerance was defined by fasting glucose ≥110 mg/dL, HbA1c ≥6.0%, or current treatment. Multivariable logistic regression (REI≥5 with BMI) and six-variable linear regression (age, sex, BMI, REI≥5, PSQI-J, JESS) were applied. REI≥5 was found in 49.3% of participants. It was associated with glucose intolerance (crude OR 7.6, 95%CI 1.5-37.3, p=0.006), and the link held after adjusting for BMI (adjusted OR 5.49, 1.02-29.57, p=0.047). REI did not correlate with JESS (r=-0.046). For identifying REI≥5, the area under the ROC curve (95%CI) was 0.419 (0.285-0.552) for JESS, 0.737 (0.619-0.855) for BMI, and 0.769 (0.660-0.877) for age. In the regression for absolute presenteeism (model F p=0.005), REI≥5 (β=-0.298, p=0.036) and PSQI-J (β=-0.264, p=0.027) were independent predictors. JESS predicted absenteeism (β=0.250, p=0.040). Mild or greater SAS was associated with glucose intolerance and with lower presenteeism, whereas sleepiness- and obesity-based indices discriminated poorly. These cross-sectional findings suggest that objective sleep testing merits prospective evaluation as an adjunct to workplace health checkups.

papers.title: Signatures of Performance Monitoring in Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder and At-risk Groups: Midfrontal Theta Predicts Divergent Behavioral Adaptation.
papers.abstract: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) has been robustly linked to increased performance monitoring, most consistently indexed by an increased error-related negativity (ERN). However, the role of response-related midfrontal theta oscillations, a key neural mechanism supporting cognitive control and behavioral adaptation, remains incompletely understood in OCD and at-risk populations. EEG was recorded from 180 adults (46 OCD, 39 unaffected first-degree relatives, 39 with adverse childhood experiences, and 56 controls) during an arrowhead flanker task. Response-related midfrontal theta power (4-7 Hz) was investigated alongside behavioral indices, including error rates and post-error slowing. Group differences in neural and behavioral data, trial-wise theta-behavior relationship, and associations with clinical symptoms were investigated. Error-related increases in midfrontal theta were robust across participants. Relative to the combined non-OCD sample, individuals with OCD exhibited enhanced error-related theta power, while unaffected first-degree relatives and individuals with adverse childhood experiences did not differ from controls. Single-trial analyses revealed altered neural-behavioral coupling: greater theta predicted slower and less accurate performance on subsequent trials in OCD, and, contrarily, improved subsequent performance in controls. Consistent with these findings, individuals with OCD showed prolonged post-error slowing. Across participants, error rate and PES were associated with worry and depressive symptoms, whereas theta power was associated with age and depressive symptoms. OCD is characterized by enhanced error-related midfrontal theta together with an altered association between neural error signals and adaptive behavioral adjustment. These findings suggest that abnormal performance monitoring in OCD reflects not only exaggerated error processing but also disrupted implementation of cognitive control.
papers.journal: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging

papers.title: From Variability to Synchrony: Non-linear Development of Auditory Neural Responses During the First Year of Life.
papers.abstract: In humans, the first year of life is characterized by rapid developmental changes, including substantial brain maturation. As a result, neural responses to auditory stimuli undergo marked changes during this period. In this study, we followed 69 infants across their first year of life and recorded high-density electroencephalography (hdEEG) at 2 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months postpartum. Infants were presented with pure beep tones to examine the development of neural responses to auditory stimulation. We analyzed event-related potentials (ERPs), inter-trial phase coherence (ITPC), and event-related spectral perturbation (ERSP) responses to the beep tones and controlled for arousal state during stimulus presentation. We found that with increasing age, neural responses became more pronounced and showed reduced trial-to-trial variability. Phase synchronization increased from 2 weeks to later developmental stages in a broad low-frequency range (0.5 Hz to 13.6 Hz), indicating improved temporal alignment of brain responses over time. However, phase synchronization decreased from 6 to 12 months, suggesting a developmental transition towards more differentiated brain activity. Taken together, these findings demonstrate that auditory maturation during the first year of life follows a non-linear trajectory driven by dynamic changes in neural synchronization, reflecting the progressive refinement of functional neural circuits. Our results thus provide a critical benchmark for understanding the neural dynamics underlying sensory development during this period.

papers.title: A connectome and transcriptome identity shift through a single transcription factor isoform.
papers.abstract: The brain exhibits remarkable neuronal diversity. The sheer number of cell types emerging from extensive transcriptional, morphological, and connectome datasets provokes the question of how the brain is capable of generating so many unique identities. Proper neuronal specification and subsequent features of identity, such as wiring, are essential for normal cognitive and behavioral function. However, we still know little about how identity and wiring are encoded within developmental programs. Here, we turn to the visual system of Drosophila melanogaster. We use its unprecedented combination of single-synapse-resolution wiring diagrams from electron microscopy (EM) connectomes and developmental gene expression profiles from single-cell transcriptomic atlases to study the molecular basis of cell-type-specific terminal identity specification and downstream wiring patterns. We integrate analyses of neuronal anatomy, whole-cell electrophysiology, and single-cell RNA sequencing after perturbation (scRNA-Perturb-seq) to establish that the transcription factor broad functions to control terminal features of identity between two visual projection neuron cell types, LPLC1 and LPLC2. We demonstrate the first characterization in functional connectivity changes following changes in neuronal identity specification. We find broad acts through a single isoform (broad-z4) that is selectively expressed in LPLC1 and has the capacity to reprogram the morphology, functional connectivity, and transcriptional identity of postmitotic LPLC2 neurons into an LPLC1-like cell type. Our findings establish a single transcription factor isoform as the smallest unit required to differentiate neuronal identity, a strategy that may be conserved within developmental programs to expand the capacity for cell-type diversity across animal species.

papers.title: Microbial bile acid deconjugation counters metabolic decline in aging.
papers.abstract: Interventions such as caloric restriction and time-restricted feeding improve lifespan and aging-associated metabolic health, in part through effects on the gut microbiome and bile acid dynamics. However, how aging alters microbial function and bile acid signaling, and whether these changes can be therapeutically leveraged, remain unclear. Here, we show that aged mice exhibit increased deconjugation of taurine-conjugated bile acids accompanied by increased bile salt hydrolase (BSH)-related transcriptional activity. Individuals with exceptional longevity show a similar bile acid deconjugation signature, suggesting an association with resilient or exceptional aging. Using engineered native bacteria, we further increased luminal BSH activity in aged mice and improved insulin sensitivity, accompanied by supportive changes in body composition and other metabolic readouts. Together, these findings suggest that elevated BSH activity may have a protective role during aging. They challenge the view that age-related changes in bile acid biotransformations are uniformly detrimental, highlighting microbial bile acid modulation as a potential strategy to improve late-life metabolic health.

papers.title: Neural mitochondria size is negatively correlated with sleep duration.
papers.abstract: Discharge of fruit fly sleep-promoting neurons is coupled to mitochondrial activity1. In vertebrates, adenosine accumulation resulting from adenosine triphosphate metabolization triggers sleep2. Such observations and theoretical considerations3,4 prompted us to investigate the link between neural mitochondria and sleep duration. To this end, we measured mitochondrial cross-sections in electron microscopy micrographs from publications of nerve or brain mitochondria in 51 mammalian species. There was considerable within-species variability of mitochondrial cross-section areas and we only included species where measurements from at least two publications could be made. Across 50 of the 51 species the average neural mitochondrial cross-section area decreased roughly exponentially with sleep duration (r = -0.76, p < 0.0001). The naked mole rat was an outlier having large brain mitochondria and long sleep. We also observed a significant decrease of sleep duration with body weight, and a multiple linear regression using sleep duration and body weight explained about 64% of the variance of mitochondrial cross-section areas. We suggest that the urge to sleep might be biophysically linked to mitochondrial size and mitochondrial leakage. Specifically, size-related decreases of mitochondrial surface-to-volume-ratio might reduce the need for sleep by decreasing mitochondrial leakage of reactive oxygen species (ROS). We identify neural mitochondrial size as a possible cellular determinant of sleep duration.

papers.title: Sensitivity of ECG QRS complexes to His-Purkinje structure in whole-heart electrophysiology models.
papers.abstract: A critical, yet understudied, determinant of patient-specific whole-heart electrophysiology (EP) model accuracy is the His-Purkinje system (HPS). The HPS influences ventricular depolarization and shapes the QRS complex of the electrocardiogram (ECG). In this study, we investigate how structural variations in the HPS models affect simulated QRS morphology for a complete whole-heart monodomain EP model, which includes all components of the cardiac conduction system. Using a rule-based fractal-tree algorithm, we generated HPS models and systematically varied nine structural parameters to evaluate their influence on ten QRS-related metrics. We used Sobol sensitivity analysis to quantify both direct effects and parameter interactions that drive observed variability in QRS metrics. Our results indicate that most minor perturbations in HPS structural parameters have limited impact on simulated QRS features. The variability induced by parameter perturbations across the 22,528 trials was neither substantially greater than the intrinsic stochastic variability of the network generation algorithm nor outside the bounds of normal QRS complexes. However, a small number of outlier trials deviated significantly. In particular, some generated HPS networks were overly dense and extended into the atrial region, leading to premature QRS complex formation, and a few others produced abnormal branching configurations that failed to adequately cover the ventricular circumference, resulting in abnormal QRS wave amplitudes and durations. These atypical HPS networks were extremely rare (<1% of the 22,528 models run) and could be readily identified and excluded from further use through quick visual inspection. Diagnostically relevant features of simulated QRS complexes in monodomain whole-heart electrophysiology models exhibited low sensitivity to moderate variations in HPS structural parameters in a healthy heart under sinus rhythm. Thus, a well-defined, generic HPS geometry is likely sufficient for most simulations of physiologically normal hearts in sinus rhythm, though some care should be taken to avoid abnormal, unphysiological networks revealed in this study. These findings represent a crucial step toward developing cardiac models that are robust to underlying anatomical uncertainties, ultimately enhancing their reliability for both research and clinical applications.
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine

papers.title: Craniofacial anatomy and obstructive sleep apnea: A systematic review of anatomical associations, airway changes, and functional outcomes.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is common in individuals with craniofacial syndromes, but the anatomical features that distinguish patients with OSA from those without remain poorly defined. We conducted a systematic review to examine the relationship between craniofacial anatomy and OSA across three domains: anatomical features associated with OSA, anatomical characteristics associated with airway dimensions, and surgical anatomical changes associated with improvements in polysomnographic outcomes. A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyzes-guided systematic review of PubMed, Embase and SCOPUS identified studies evaluating craniofacial and upper-airway anatomy in relation to OSA or surgical outcomes in patients with craniofacial syndromes. Anatomical and OSA outcomes were extracted, synthesized, and appraised using study-design-appropriate risk-of-bias tools. Twelve studies comprising 283 patients were included; Crouzon (n = 127) and Apert (n = 74) syndromes accounted for 77% of the cohort. Five studies evaluated anatomical features associated with OSA, including upper-airway length, posterior airway space, retropalatal cross-sectional area, and midfacial dimensions. Midface advancement consistently increased nasopharyngeal, velopharyngeal, and upper-airway dimensions. Functional outcomes were more variable: greater horizontal advancement was associated with greater Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) improvement in one study, whereas airway-volume expansion did not consistently correspond to AHI improvement, and residual OSA persisted in some patients despite anatomical improvement. Anatomical features may identify patients at increased risk for OSA; however, these predictors require external validation before they can be applied clinically. Furthermore, although midface advancement improves airway anatomy and OSA severity, anatomical improvement does not reliably correspond to OSA resolution. Therefore, postoperative imaging cannot substitute for polysomnography when assessing function.
papers.journal: Journal of plastic, reconstructive & aesthetic surgery : JPRAS

papers.title: Acupuncture versus conventional therapy for painful temporomandibular disorders in women: a study protocol for an assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: The prevalence of temporomandibular disorder (TMD) has been increasing, and its high rate of chronicity makes it a relevant public health concern. Despite the availability of several treatment options, there is still no consensus regarding the most effective approach for managing painful TMD. This study presents the protocol for an assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial designed to evaluate the effectiveness of acupuncture compared with conventional treatment in patients with painful TMD. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: (1) systemic individualized acupuncture based on Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) diagnosis; (2) local acupuncture according to Western diagnostic criteria; or (3) standard treatment consisting of oral splint therapy and pharmacotherapy. TMD will be assessed using the DC/TMD Axis I protocol. Evaluations will be performed at baseline, after the intervention period, and at 3- and 6-month follow-ups. All treatment protocols will last eight weeks. The primary outcome is pain intensity, assessed by the Numeric Rating Scale. Secondary outcomes include pain interference in daily life, jaw functional limitation, oral behaviors, anxiety, depression, and somatization (DC/TMD Axis II instruments). Sleep quality will be evaluated using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, and salivary cortisol levels will serve as an exploratory physiological biomarker associated with stress response. Data collection and analysis are ongoing; results will determine comparative treatment efficacy across all groups. This is the first clinical trial to compare individualized acupuncture based on TCM with a standardized acupuncture protocol derived from Western diagnosis in the management of painful TMD. The findings are expected to contribute to evidence-based clinical practice and improve therapeutic decision-making for this complex condition.
papers.journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine

papers.title: In vivo probabilistic atlas mapping reveals brainstem nuclei volume increases in idiopathic REM sleep behavior disorder.
papers.abstract: Idiopathic rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) serves as a key prodromal marker of synucleinopathies, and its core symptoms are closely associated with brainstem pathology. Nevertheless, in vivo imaging research on brainstem nuclei in iRBD patients is still limited due to methodological constraints. This study aimed to explore volume changes of brainstem nuclei in iRBD patients via a fine-grained probabilistic atlas, and analyze their clinical correlations and diagnostic value. We enrolled 3D T1-weighted MRI data of 178 iRBD patients and 111 healthy controls from the PPMI database. After preprocessing, 54 brainstem nuclei were segmented using the Brainstem Navigator atlas, and their relative volumes were compared between groups with multiple comparison correction. Correlation analyses with clinical scales and ROC analyses were conducted for nuclei with significant inter-group differences. Compared to HCs, iRBD patients presented significantly enlarged relative volumes in the left cuneiform nucleus, left lateral parabrachial nucleus, and left superior medullary reticular formation. The volumes of the latter two nuclei were positively correlated with RBDSQ scores and related to autonomic, affective and cognitive indicators. The AUC of single nucleus for iRBD diagnosis ranged from 0.607 to 0.637, while the combined model reached 0.674. These findings confirm volumetric enlargement in specific brainstem nuclei of iRBD patients, suggesting early pathological remodeling in these regions. They clarify the brainstem structural basis of iRBD symptoms and suggest that brainstem nuclei volumes, with moderate discriminative performance, may serve as supplementary imaging markers to complement clinical assessments in iRBD.

papers.title: Joint associations of sleep duration and screen time with mental health symptoms among 10,620 Chinese university students: An exploratory cross-sectional dose-response analysis.
papers.abstract: Psychological distress is common among university students and is associated with modifiable lifestyle factors. This study examined the joint associations of sleep duration and screen time with mental health symptoms and explored whether physical activity (PA) dose-response patterns varied across sleep-screen profiles. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 10,620 Chinese university students (mean age 19.8 ± 1.3 years). Sleep timing, screen time, and PA were assessed using self-report questionnaires, and depression, anxiety, and stress symptoms were assessed using the DASS-21. Multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline models were used to estimate associations and explore dose-response patterns. Prevalence rates were 43.7% for depression, 40.7% for anxiety, and 17.6% for stress symptoms. Combined short sleep (<7.0 h/day) and high screen time (>8.0 h/day) was associated with higher odds of depression (OR = 1.68), anxiety (OR = 1.86), and stress symptoms (OR = 2.31) than the reference profile (7.0-9.0 h sleep and < 4.0 h screen time). Exploratory PA dose-response patterns varied across sleep-screen profiles, with substantial uncertainty in several subgroups. Short sleep and high screen time were jointly associated with higher odds of psychological symptoms. Context-specific PA curve features were exploratory and require confirmation in longitudinal and intervention studies before they can inform behavioral recommendations.

papers.title: A novel theta-frequency tACS approach for major depressive disorder: Initial findings from an open-label pilot study.
papers.abstract: Theta oscillations are implicated in the pathophysiology of major depressive disorder (MDD) and represent a promising neuromodulation target. This study investigates individualized theta-frequency (ITF) transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) in adults with moderate-to-severe MDD, and reports on the initial evaluation of feasibility, tolerability, and clinical and neurophysiological outcomes. In this open-label pilot study, adults with MDD underwent a 20-session course of theta-frequency tACS (1.5 mA peak-to-peak; 20 min/session) applied bilaterally over the prefrontal cortex while performing working memory tasks. Theta stimulation frequency was individualized from pretreatment task-based electroencephalography (EEG) and recalibrated after 10 sessions. Montgomery-Asberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) and EEG were assessed at baseline, midpoint (2weeks), and endpoint (4weeks), with MADRS repeated at 4-week follow-up. Ten of 11 enrolled participants completed all 20 treatment sessions and were included in analyses. Reported side effects were mild and transient. MADRS scores decreased significantly from baseline to midpoint, endpoint, and follow-up. At endpoint, response and remission rates were 80% and 60%, respectively; at follow-up, rates were 80% and 70% respectively. Greater increases in individualized theta frequency (ITF) power were associated with greater reductions in MADRS scores, although no significant group-level changes in ITF power were observed. The open-label design, absence of a sham comparator, and small sample size warrant cautious interpretation of these initial observations, particularly given the potential influence of placebo and expectancy effects. This pilot evaluation of individualized theta-frequency tACS in MDD demonstrates the feasibility of this novel approach and provides preliminary clinical and neurophysiological observations to inform future sham-controlled trials.

papers.title: Space-by-time semi-NMF: A decomposition approach for single-trial neural decoding.
papers.abstract: The activity of populations of sensory neurons is assumed to encode stimulusinformation across both spatial and temporal dimensions, reflecting differences in tuningacross neurons and variations in their responses over time. With the rapid expansionof simultaneously recorded neural populations in electrophysiological experiments, thereis an increasing demand for analytical frameworks capable of compactly capturing thismultidimensional sensory information within single-trial population activity, particularlyunder conditions of high baseline activity. To address this, we developed anovel analytical method that decomposes neural activity into spatial firing patterns (co-firingneuron ensembles), temporal firing patterns (temporal dynamics of these groups of neurons),and trial-dependent activation coefficients (strength of recruitment of such firing patternson each trial). This method extends the space-by-time nonnegative matrix factorization(SbT-NMF), a tensor decomposition that imposes nonnegativity constraints on all factorizedmatrices and is suitable for inherently nonnegative data such as neural activity by relaxingthe nonnegativity constraint on one matrix. This modification enables the application of animportant baseline correction, which involves subtracting prestimulus activity from the data.As a result, the input may contain negative values, reflecting deviations from baseline andthereby reducing the influence of ongoing activity before the stimulus. Weapplied this refined method to primary visual cortex data from the Allen Brain Instituteand found that SbT-sNMF (66% ± 0.7%) achieved a 32% relative increase in stimulusdecoding performance over the original SbT-NMF (50% ± 1.4%). Thesefindings highlight the importance of accounting for baseline correction to achieve compactand linearly decodable low-dimensional representation of neural population dynamics in ourproposed frameworks.

papers.title: Comparison and extension of the Riemannian Procrustes analysis and tangent space alignment transfer learning methods.
papers.abstract: This study compares Riemannian Procrustes analysis (RPA) and tangent space alignment (TSA) for transfer learning of motor-imagery EEG data. The study also examines how performance changes when the EEG data is represented using analytic Hermitian positive definite covariance matrices instead of standard symmetric positive definite covariance matrices.Approach. The methods' geometric constraints were compared and explained. Additionally, the methods were evaluated in two scenarios on real EEG data, one with substantial target-domain knowledge and one calibration-like with a limited amount of training data and thus limited target-domain knowledge. Six public EEG datasets with multiple subjects performing two or multiple motor imagery tasks were used. We report paired comparisons of classification performance for the different transfer learning methods and covariance matrix representations across the datasets in order to draw general conclusions about performance.Main results. In the scenario with substantial target-domain knowledge, the TSA method outperformed the RPA method, and representing the EEG data as analytical covariance matrices outperformed standard covariance matrices. In the scenario with limited target-domain knowledge, performance depended on the amount of available target data, and source-data selection emerged as an important component of successful transfer learning. Significance. This study gives a deeper understanding of TSA and RPA transfer learning methods commonly used in brain-computer interfaces, which may inform future research and implementation. The analysis also demonstrates the importance of source data selection in brain-computer interface transfer learning.

papers.title: Association between sleep quality and symptoms of depression and anxiety among older Korean Americans: the role of social isolation.
papers.abstract: Older Korean Americans living in low-income senior housing often face sleep problems that may be linked to elevated symptoms of depression and anxiety. This study aims to examine associations between sleep quality/change in sleep quality and symptoms of depression and anxiety in this group. We also examined a potential effect modification by social isolation. We analyzed survey data from 310 Korean Americans aged 65 and older in Los Angeles senior housing sites, measuring sleep quality and change, symptoms of depression and anxiety, social isolation, and other sociodemographic characteristics. Linear regression models assessed the relationships between sleep quality/change in sleep quality and symptoms of depression and anxiety, adjusting for age, gender, marital status, education, employment status, and financial need met by income. We also tested the moderating effect of social isolation. Poor sleep quality was associated with a 3.93-point increase in depressive symptoms and a 2.67-point increase in anxiety symptoms, adjusting for covariates. Negative change in sleep quality was associated with a 3.86-point increase in depressive symptoms and 2.41-point increase in anxiety symptoms in the multivariate-adjusted model. Social isolation was a significant effect modifier: The sleep quality and depressive symptoms association was stronger among socially isolated participants. Our study highlights significant associations between sleep quality/negative change in sleep quality and symptoms of depression and anxiety in older Korean Americans residing in subsidized senior housing. It further underscores the potential vulnerability of socially isolated individuals to the negative mental health impacts of poor sleep.

papers.title: Efficacy of a social zeitgeber theory-based intervention targeting social rhythm, role adaptation, and sleep cognition for sleep disturbances among people living with HIV/AIDS in China: A randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: People living with HIV/AIDS (PLWHA) commonly experience sleep disturbances that may be associated with disrupted social rhythms and HIV-related psychosocial stressors. Existing interventions show inconsistent effects, and few address these factors within a theoretically integrated framework. This study evaluated a social zeitgeber theory-based intervention adapted from Interpersonal and Social Rhythm Therapy to improve sleep quality. In a randomized controlled trial in China, 102 PLWHA were randomized 1:1 to intervention or waitlist control. The intervention targeted social rhythm stabilization, HIV-related role adaptation, and maladaptive sleep beliefs. Sleep quality, social rhythm, depressive symptoms, and sleep cognition were assessed at baseline, post-intervention, and 3-month follow-up. Generalized estimating equations assessed intervention effects under intention-to-treat, and longitudinal mediation analyses examined potential pathways. Compared with controls, the intervention group showed greater improvements in sleep quality at post-intervention (B = -2.98, SE = 0.56, 95% CI: -4.08 to -1.88) and 3-month follow-up (B = -2.94, SE = 0.65, 95% CI: -4.22 to -1.66). Social rhythm, depressive symptoms, and sleep cognition also improved at both assessments. Indirect effects on sleep quality were observed through social rhythm (B = -0.672, SE = 0.251, 95% CI: -1.309 to -0.297), depressive symptoms (B = -0.696, SE = 0.269, 95% CI: -1.381 to -0.284), and sleep cognition (B = -0.976, SE = 0.341, 95% CI: -1.759 to -0.405). The intervention produced sustained improvements in sleep quality. Social rhythm, depressive symptoms, and sleep cognition emerged as potential pathways, supporting theoretically integrated and contextually adapted approaches to HIV sleep care.
